BURHAN:v3p437/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p437/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p437/r4.claim: A reinforced metaphor attends to the source image: ربحت تجارتهم extends the buying image in اشتروا الضلالة بالهدى with matching terms of profit and trade.
BURHAN:v3p437/r4.anchor: تنقسم إلى مرشحة وهي أحسنها وهي أن تنظر إلى جانب المستعار وتراعيه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p314/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p314/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p314/r5.claim: Saying their trade did not profit is not rhetorically equal to saying they did not profit in their trade.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p314/r5.anchor: لا يروا فرقا بين قوله تعالى : ( ﴿ فما ربحت تجارتهم ﴾ ) وبين : فما ربحوا في تجارتهم

QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#2/r1.claim: The people of Paradise trade worldly life for the afterlife, while the people of the Fire trade the afterlife for worldly life; this is figurative exchange and loss.
QURTUBI-FULL:64:9#2/r1.anchor: أهل الجنة اشتروا الآخرة بترك الدنيا، واشترى أهل النار الدنيا بترك الآخرة

BURSEVI:v1p48#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p48#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p48#2/r5.claim: The demonstrative points emphatically to the hypocrites and signals their remote, exceptionally evil condition; it is the subject whose predicate is that they exchanged misguidance for guidance.
BURSEVI:v1p48#2/r5.anchor: المنافقون المتصفون بما ذكر من الصفات الشنيعة المميزة لهم

BURSEVI:v1p48#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p48#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p48#2/r6.claim: Buying first means paying a price, then metaphorically giving up what one holds to obtain something else; here they chose unbelief and deviation instead of faith and the straight path.
BURSEVI:v1p48#2/r6.anchor: أصل الاشتراء بذل الثمن لتحصيل ما يطلب من الأشياء ثم استعير للإعراض عما في يده محصلا به غيره

BURSEVI:v1p49/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p49/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p49/r1.claim: In an exchange, bāʾ accompanies what is relinquished; this supports establishing a legal ruling through conduct without spoken offer and acceptance.
BURSEVI:v1p49/r1.anchor: والباء تصحب المتروك في باب المعارضة وهذا دليل على أن الحكم يثبت بالتعاطي من غير تكلم بالإيجاب والقبول

BURSEVI:v1p49/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p49/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p49/r2.claim: Calling the trade unprofitable extends the metaphor: profit belongs literally to traders, but is attributed to their trade as its agent or cause; the fa implies that their purchase yielded no gain.
BURSEVI:v1p49/r2.anchor: فإن الربح مسند إلى أرباب التجارة في الحقيقة فإسناده إلى التجارة نفسها على الاتساع لتلبسها بالفاعل

BURSEVI:v1p49/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p49/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p49/r3.claim: Trade seeks a surplus over its capital; even a lost deal can be recovered while capital remains, but the hypocrites destroyed both their sound nature and clear reason, leaving no means to reach truth or perfection.
BURSEVI:v1p49/r3.anchor: فإن المقصد منها سلامة رأس المال مع حصول الربح ولئن فات الربح في صفقة فربما يتدارك في صفقة أخرى

BURSEVI:v1p49/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p49/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p49/r4.claim: True guidance requires leaving worldly habits for obedience and worship, rather than following every desire and mixing whim with guidance.
BURSEVI:v1p49/r4.anchor: هو الذي ترك الدنيا والعادة ثم اشتغل بوظائف الطاعة والعبادة

BURSEVI:v1p49/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p49/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p49/r5.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Daqqāq tells a wealthy disciple that voluntary night prayer will not cure him while love of worldly life remains; he must first remove that love, then take up extra worship.
BURSEVI:v1p49/r5.anchor: حكي أنه كان للشيخ الأستاذ أبي علي الدقاق رضي الله عنه مريد تاجر متمول

BURSEVI:v1p49/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p49/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p49/r6.claim: The shaykh compares misdirected spiritual treatment to applying ointment to a foot for a headache or washing a garment’s hem to cleanse a dirty hand.
BURSEVI:v1p49/r6.anchor: فمن كان به أذى من رأسه من صداع لا يسكن ألمه بالطلاء على الرجل

BURSEVI:v1p50/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p50/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p50/r1.claim: Squandering the two gains leaves a complete veil from God, rusting over the heart, as the Qurʾān says.
BURSEVI:v1p50/r1.anchor: وخسرانهم بإضاعة الأمرين هو الحجاب الكلي عن الحق بالرين

BURSEVI:v1p50/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p50/r2.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v1p50/r2.claim: Their tyranny and confusion make them content with worldly life and saturate their hearts with misguidance; the resulting state comes from their own transaction.
BURSEVI:v1p50/r2.anchor: التأويلات النجمية" الإشارة في الآية أن من نتيجة طغيانهم

BURSEVI:v1p50/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p50/r3.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v1p50/r3.claim: They gave up their capacity to receive guidance, so they cannot regain it; preferring the world to the afterlife is a loss, but preferring both to God is worse, leaving them captive to desire and cut off from the Beloved.
BURSEVI:v1p50/r3.anchor: لأنهم أخرجوا استعداد قبول الهداية عن قدرتهم وتصرفهم فلا يملكون الرجوع إليه

BURSEVI:v1p50/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p50/r4.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v1p50/r4.claim: They are not guided because they invalidated their good innate readiness to accept guidance.

QASHANI:2:15-16#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:15-16#2/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:15-16#2/r1.claim: Purchased misguidance is darkness and veiling from truth or religion, against guidance by original potential light.
QASHANI:2:15-16#2/r1.anchor: أي: الظلمة، والاحتجاب عن طريق الحق الذي هو الدين، أو عن الحق.

QASHANI:2:15-16#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:15-16#2/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:15-16#2/r2.claim: Their capital of light and permanence should have earned perfected light through knowledge, works, gnosis, wisdom, and virtuous character, bringing real wealth and nearness to God.
QASHANI:2:15-16#2/r2.anchor: إذ كان رأس مالهم من عالم النور والبقاء ليكتسبوا به ما يجانسه من النور الفيضي الكمالي

QASHANI:2:15-16#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:15-16#2/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:15-16#2/r3.claim: They squandered original guidance by eroding preparedness and clouding their hearts, causing eternal veiling, deprivation, and loss.
QASHANI:2:15-16#2/r3.anchor: وضاعت الهداية الأصلية التي كانت بضاعتهم ورأس مالهم بإزالة استعدادهم وتكدير قلوبهم بالرين الموجب للحجاب والحرمان الأبدي

AKHFASH:v1p50/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p50/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p50/r2.claim: In اشتروا, the wāw must remain because dropping it would hide the plural; its ḍamma represents the omitted element's ḍamma.
AKHFASH:v1p50/r2.anchor: انما حركتها بالضم لان الحرف الذي ذهب من الكلمة مضموم، فصار يقوم مقامه

AKHFASH:v1p50/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p50/r3.speaker: some Arabs
AKHFASH:v1p50/r3.claim: Some Arabs read اشتروا with kasra after two vowelless letters; al-Akhfash calls this a rare dialect form.
AKHFASH:v1p50/r3.anchor: لما وجدوا حرفا ساكنا قد لقي ساكنا كسروا كما يكسرون في غير هذا الموضع

AKHFASH:v1p52#2/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p52#2/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p52#2/r1.claim: فما ربحت تجارتهم is an attribution to the trade; the intended sense is that they themselves did not profit from it.
AKHFASH:v1p52#2/r1.anchor: قوله {فما ربحت تجارتهم} فهذا على قول العرب: "خاب سعيك" وانما هو الذي خاب، وانما يريد "فما ربحوا في تجارتهم"

AKHFASH:v1p52#2/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p52#2/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p52#2/r2.claim: The author compares this ellipsis to بل مكر الليل والنهار and ولكن البر من آمن بالله, where an understood noun is supplied.
AKHFASH:v1p52#2/r2.anchor: ومثله {بل مكر الليل والنهار} [و] {ولكن البر من آمن بالله} انما هو "ولكن البر بر من آمن بالله"

AKHFASH:v1p52#2/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p52#2/r3.speaker: الشاعر
AKHFASH:v1p52#2/r3.claim: The first poem is cited as evidence for omitted or displaced nominal wording; the words quoted are كيف تواصل.
AKHFASH:v1p52#2/r3.anchor: وكيف تواصل من أصبحت خلالته كأبي مرحب

AKHFASH:v1p52#2/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p52#2/r4.speaker: الشاعر
AKHFASH:v1p52#2/r4.claim: The second poem is explained as meaning the worst deaths include the death of a person among his family; منية is understood before ميت.
AKHFASH:v1p52#2/r4.anchor: انما يريد "وشر المنايا منية ميت وسط اهله

AKHFASH:v1p52#2/r5.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p52#2/r5.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p52#2/r5.claim: Phrases such as أكثر شربي الماء mean drinking water and eating bread, not drinking by water or eating by bread.
AKHFASH:v1p52#2/r5.anchor: ومثله: "اكثر شربي الماء" و "أكثر أكلي الخبر" وليس أكلك بالخبز ولا شربك بالماء

AKHFASH:v1p52#2/r6.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p52#2/r6.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p52#2/r6.claim: واسأل القرية means ask its people, and العير means the owners of the caravan.
AKHFASH:v1p52#2/r6.anchor: قال {وسئل القرية} يريد: "أهل القرية"، (والعير) أي: "واسأل اصحاب العير"

AKHFASH:v1p52#2/r7.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p52#2/r7.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p52#2/r7.claim: He analyzes مثل الذين كفروا كمثل الذي ينعق as compressed wording: your likeness and theirs is like caller and called-to; omitted words are understood from what remains.
AKHFASH:v1p52#2/r7.anchor: فانما هو - والله اعلم - "مثلكم ومثل الذين كفروا كمثل الناعق والمنعوق به"

AKHFASH:v1p52#2/r8.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p52#2/r8.speaker: some
AKHFASH:v1p52#2/r8.claim: Some instead compare the disbelievers' invocation of their gods to a caller shouting at sheep, since neither gods nor sheep hear or understand.
AKHFASH:v1p52#2/r8.anchor: وقد قال بعضهم {ومثل الذين كفروا كمثل الذي ينعق} يقول "مثلهم في دعائهم الآلهة كمثل الذي ينعق بالغنم"

FARRA:v1p14/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p14/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p14/r1.claim: Context can license an understood pronoun; al-Farrāʾ says this kind of omission is common in Arabic and poetry.
FARRA:v1p14/r1.anchor: فحسن الإضمار لما عرف. ومثله فى سورة الواقعة

FARRA:v1p14/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p14/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p14/r2.claim: An omitted pronoun is unsuitable when the coordinated actions have no close semantic connection to identify what was left out.
FARRA:v1p14/r2.anchor: وأما ما لا يحسن فيه الضمير لقلة اجتماعه

FARRA:v1p14/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p14/r3.speaker: بعض بني أسد
FARRA:v1p14/r3.claim: An anonymous man of Banū Asad recited a horse poem as Arabic poetic evidence for the preceding construction.
FARRA:v1p14/r3.anchor: وأنشدني بعض بني أسد يصف فرسه:

FARRA:v1p14/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p14/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p14/r4.claim: The phrase says the trade profited although merchants, not trade itself, profit; the meaning is clear from the commercial context.
FARRA:v1p14/r4.anchor: كيف تربح التجارة وإنما يربح الرجل التاجر؟

FARRA:v1p14/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p14/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p14/r5.claim: Arabic idiom permits attributing profit or loss to a sale, as well as describing a night as sleeping or a matter as resolved.
FARRA:v1p14/r5.anchor: فحسن القول بذلك لأن الربح والخسران إنما يكونان

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p42/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p42/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p42/r1.claim: اشتروا الضلالة بالهدى means they exchanged guidance for error; buying one thing with another is fundamentally an exchange.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p42/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p42/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p42/r2.claim: The phrase makes trade profit although profit belongs to its participants; this is figurative language, like saying the matter was resolved.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p42/r2.anchor: والتجارة لا تربح، وإنما يربح فيها

NAHHAS:v1p191/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p191/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p191/r3.claim: In أولئك الذين اشتروا, أولئك is the subject and الذين its predicate; اشتروا الضلالة بالهدى is the relative clause.
NAHHAS:v1p191/r3.anchor: مبتدأ ( الذين ) خبر ( اشتروا الضلالة بالهدى ) في صلة الذين

NAHHAS:v1p191/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p191/r4.speaker: سيبويه
NAHHAS:v1p191/r4.claim: Sibawayh says the wāw in اشتروا takes damma to distinguish it from an original wāw; he compares وأن لو استقاموا.
NAHHAS:v1p191/r4.anchor: قول سيبويه أنها ضم فرقا بينها

NAHHAS:v1p191/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p191/r5.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v1p191/r5.claim: Al-Farra says the plural wāw originally followed another wāw; after the first dropped, the remaining wāw took its vowel.
NAHHAS:v1p191/r5.anchor: وقال الفراء كان يجب أن يكون قبلها واو مضمومة لأنها واو جمع

NAHHAS:v1p191/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p191/r6.speaker: ابن كيسان
NAHHAS:v1p191/r6.claim: Ibn Kaysan says damma is lighter on wāw than other vowels because it shares its articulation.
NAHHAS:v1p191/r6.anchor: قال ابن كيسان الضمة في الواو أخف من غيرها لأنها من جنسها

NAHHAS:v1p191/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p191/r7.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v1p191/r7.claim: Abu Ishaq treats it as plural wāw given damma, as also in نحن.
NAHHAS:v1p191/r7.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق هي واو جمع حركت بالضم كما فعل في نحن

NAHHAS:v1p191/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p191/r8.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق ويحيى بن يعمر
NAHHAS:v1p191/r8.claim: Ibn Abi Ishaq and Yahya ibn Yaʿmar read اشتروا with kasra, following the original form to resolve two adjacent sukūns.
NAHHAS:v1p191/r8.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي إسحاق ويحيى بن يعمر ( اشتروا الضلالة ) بكسر الواو وعلى الأصل لالتقاء الساكنين

NAHHAS:v1p191/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p191/r9.speaker: أبو زيد الأنصاري
NAHHAS:v1p191/r9.claim: Abu Zayd reports Qanab Abu al-Sammal al-Adawi reading the wāw with fatḥa for ease and agreement with the preceding fatḥa.
NAHHAS:v1p191/r9.anchor: وروى أبو زيد الأنصاري عن قعنب أبي السمال العدوي أنه قرأ ( اشتروا الضلالة ) بفتح الواو

NAHHAS:v1p191/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p191/r10.speaker: الكسائي
NAHHAS:v1p191/r10.claim: Al-Kisaʾi permits damma on the wāw, comparing forms such as أقتت and أدؤر.
NAHHAS:v1p191/r10.anchor: وأجاز الكسائي ( اشتروا الضلالة ) بضم الواو كما يقال أقتت وأدؤر

NAHHAS:v1p191/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p191/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p191/r11.claim: Al-Nahhas calls al-Kisaʾi’s analogy mistaken: hamza over wāw is allowed only when the wāw is rounded for a reason other than this one.
NAHHAS:v1p191/r11.anchor: قال أبو جعفر وهذا غلط لأن همزة الواو إذا انضمت إنما يجوز فيها إذا انضمت لغير علة

NAHHAS:v1p191/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p191/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p191/r12.claim: تجارتهم is nominative as the subject of ربحت; مهتدين is accusative as the predicate of كان.
NAHHAS:v1p191/r12.anchor: فما ربحت تجارتهم ) رفع بربحت ( وما كانوا مهتدين ) نصب على خبر كان

NAHHAS:v1p191/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p191/r13.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v1p191/r13.claim: Al-Farra allows مهتدين to be a circumstantial phrase that cannot be omitted without loss.
NAHHAS:v1p191/r13.anchor: والفراء يقول حال غير مستغنى عنها

NAHHAS:v1p191/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p191/r14.speaker: ابن كيسان
NAHHAS:v1p191/r14.claim: Ibn Kaysan permits the lexical variants تجارة or تجاير and ضلالة or ضلايل.
NAHHAS:v1p191/r14.anchor: قال ابن كيسان يجوز تجارة وتجاير وضلالة وضلايل

IBNABIHATIM:v1p49/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p49/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v1p49/r1.anchor: عن قتادة ، في قوله : اولئك الذين اشتروا الضلالة بالهدى قال : استحبوا الضلالة على الهدى

IBNABIHATIM:v1p49/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p49/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p49/r2.claim: The bargain was disbelief in exchange for faith.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p49/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس : اولئك الذين اشتروا الضلالة بالهدى اي الكفر بالايمان

IBNABIHATIM:v1p49/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p49/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v1p49/r3.claim: They first believed and then disbelieved.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p49/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد : اولئك الذين اشتروا الضلالة بالهدى امنوا ثم كفروا

IBNABIHATIM:v1p49/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p49/r4.speaker: السدى
IBNABIHATIM:v1p49/r4.claim: They took error and abandoned guidance.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p49/r4.anchor: عن السدى : اولئك الذين اشتروا الضلالة بالهدى يقول : اخذوا الضلالة وتركوا الهدى

IBNABIHATIM:v1p49/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p49/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v1p49/r5.claim: The statement that their trade did not profit and they were unguided refers to the hypocrites.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p49/r5.anchor: عن قتادة ، في قوله فما ربحت تجارتهم وما كانوا مهتدين قال : هذه في المنافقين

IBNABIHATIM:v1p49/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p49/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v1p49/r6.claim: They moved from guidance to error, unity to division, safety to fear, and the Sunna to innovation, so their trade failed and they were unguided.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p49/r6.anchor: عن قتادة ، في قوله : فما ربحت تجارتهم وما كانوا مهتدين قد - والله - رايتموهم فخرجوا من الهدى إلى الضلالة ، ومن الجماعة إلى الفرقة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p297#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p297#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p297#2/r1.claim: The demonstrative points to the people described from 2:8 onward as a collective class; the relative clause sums up their accumulated traits.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p297#2/r1.anchor: وما عطف على صلته من صفاتهم وجيء باسم إشارة الجمع لأن ما صدق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p297#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p297#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p297#2/r2.claim: The sentence is detached to restate the ending of 2:15, answer why God leaves them wandering, and conclude the preceding portrait; all three functions favor separation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p297#2/r2.anchor: وفصلت الجملة عن التي قبلها لتفيد تقرير معنى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p297#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p297#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p297#2/r3.claim: Its placement contrasts with the guidance of the God-fearing in 2:5 and the sealing of disbelievers' hearts in 2:7.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p297#2/r3.anchor: وموقع هذه الجملة من نظم الكلام مقابل موقع جملة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p297#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p297#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p297#2/r4.claim: The demonstrative refers to a category whose traits make its members seem present to the listener; it does not itself imply distance or contempt.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p297#2/r4.anchor: ليس في هذه الإشارة إشعار ببعد أو قرب حتى تفيد تحقيرا ناشئا عن البعد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p297#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p297#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p297#2/r5.claim: By contrast, using the far demonstrative for the nearby Qur'an in 2:2 signals its grandeur.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p297#2/r5.anchor: عدول عن إشارة القريب إلى البعيد فأفاد التعظيم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p297#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p297#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p297#2/r6.claim: Qays ibn al-Khaṭīm uses a near demonstrative for distant death to express contempt for it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p297#2/r6.anchor: فإن الموت بعيد عنه فحقه أن يشير إليه باسم البعيد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p298#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p298#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p298#2/r1.claim: Ishtarā can mean exchange or substitute; Bashāma ibn Ḥazn and ʿAntara ibn al-Akhras al-Maʿnī provide poetic examples of that established sense.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p298#2/r1.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الاشتراء مستعملا في الاستبدال وهو لازمه الأول واستعماله في هذا اللازم مشهور

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p298#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p298#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p298#2/r2.claim: The hypocrites' professed faith resembles guidance temporarily adopted, then discarded for their hidden misguidance; purchase is a metaphor for choosing between two states.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p298#2/r2.anchor: اختلاطهم كما اشترى المسلم إذ تنصرا بالمسلمين وإظهارهم الإيمان حالة تشبه حال المهتدي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p298#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p298#2/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p298#2/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari accepts the metaphorical reading, comparing their choice of misguidance to a buyer who takes something previously unavailable to him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p298#2/r3.anchor: وعلى هذا الوجه الثاني يصح أيضا أن يكون الاشتراء استعارة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p298#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p298#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p298#2/r4.claim: The generic relative clause rhetorically restricts the description to this group, portraying them as maximal seekers of misguidance through disbelief, folly, deceit, corruption, and mockery.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p298#2/r4.anchor: بلغوا الغاية في اشتراء الضلالة والحرص عليها إذ جمعوا الكفر والسفه والخداع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p299/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p299/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p299/r1.claim: The result clauses follow their purchase because both loss and lack of guidance become publicly evident through that act, even though lack of guidance precedes or causes it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p299/r1.anchor: رتبت الفاء عدم الربح المعطوف بها وعدم الاهتداء المعطوف عليه على اشتراء الضلالة بالهدى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p299/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p299/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p299/r2.claim: The past-tense construction mā kānū muhtadīn stresses that their failure of guidance was longstanding and deeply rooted.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p299/r2.anchor: لأن ما كانوا أبلغ في النفي لإشعاره بأن انتفاء الاهتداء عنهم أمر متأصل سابق قديم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p299/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p299/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p299/r3.claim: Trade means seeking goods to resell for gain; the metaphor depicts hypocrites pursuing an aim through hypocrisy but failing, and loss of profit implies loss of capital within the intended comparison.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p299/r3.anchor: تشبيه لحال المنافقين إذ قصدوا من النفاق غاية فأخفقت مساعيهم وضاعت مقاصدهم بحال التجار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p300/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p300/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p300/r1.claim: Profit is attributed to trade metonymically because trade causes the trader's gain; its negation is also figurative, since literal denial would state an obvious fact.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p300/r1.anchor: وإنما أسند الربح إلى التجارة حتى نفي عنها لأن الربح لما كان مسببا عن التجارة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p300/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p300/r2.speaker: التفتازاني
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p300/r2.claim: Al-Taftazani's final position in al-Muṭawwal treats the negation as figurative; Ibn ʿAshur prefers that account to the contrary view in the Kashshaf glosses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p300/r2.anchor: وهذه هي الطريقة التي انفصل عليها المحقق التفتزاني

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p300/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p300/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p300/r3.claim: The trade language reinforces the purchase metaphor; reinforcement may be a literal companion to one metaphor or a second metaphor that also has independent force.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p300/r3.anchor: فإن مرجع الترشيح إلى أن يقفى المجاز بما يناسبه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p300/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p300/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p300/r4.claim: An unattributed poem recorded by Ibn al-Aʿrābī compares gray hair to a vulture and dark hair to a crow, then extends the image by making gray hair nest in the temples.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p300/r4.anchor: ولما رأيت النسر عز ابن داية وعشش في وكريه جاش له صدري

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p301/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p301/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p301/r1.claim: A second, unattributed poem makes satanic whispering a lizard entering its burrow and counsel against it the act of drawing the lizard out; the second image depends on the first.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p301/r1.anchor: إذا الشيطان قصع في قفاها تنفقناه بالحبل التؤام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p301/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p301/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p301/r2.claim: The verse's no-guidance clause is not redundant: guidance in the exchange metaphor is religious, while the denied guidance is ordinary knowledge of the route to one's aim.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p301/r2.anchor: فتعين أن الاهتداء المنفي هو الاهتداء بالمعنى الأصلي في اللغة وهو معرفة الطريق الموصل للمقصود

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p301/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p301/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p301/r3.claim: Their lack of guidance figuratively exposes wasted aims and foolish judgment: they failed to find what benefits the afterlife or protects Muslims, losing both gain and capital.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p301/r3.anchor: ومعنى نفي الاهتداء كناية عن إضاعة القصد أي إنهم أضاعوا ما سعوا له

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p97#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p97#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p97#2/r7.claim: Awlāʾika begins a nominal sentence, alladhīna is its predicate, and ishtaraw is the relative clause; the verb is morphologically explained from ishtariyū through vowel change and deletion.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p98/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p98/r1.speaker: أبو علي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p98/r1.claim: Abū ʿAlī says ḍamma on the plural wāw in ishtaraw helps distinguish it from wāw in aw or law, whose vowels are kasra.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p98/r1.anchor: الضم فيها أولى ليفصل بينها وبين واو

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p98/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p98/r2.speaker: أبو السمال قعنب العدوي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p98/r2.claim: Abū al-Sammāl Qunb reads ishtaraw with fatḥa on wāw.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p98/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو السمال قعنب العدوي بفتح الواو

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p98/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p98/r3.speaker: يحيى بن يعمر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p98/r3.claim: Yaḥyā b. Yaʿmar reads ishtaraw with kasra on wāw.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p98/r3.anchor: وقرأها يحيى بن يعمر بكسر الواو

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p98/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p98/r4.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p98/r4.claim: Some gloss “they purchased misguidance for guidance” as taking misguidance and abandoning guidance; others say they preferred misguidance and shunned guidance, as in 41:17.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p98/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p98/r5.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p98/r5.claim: Others take purchase as a metaphor: guidance was available but they chose misguidance in its place, as if they paid their guidance for it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p98/r5.anchor: شبهوا بمن اشترى فكأنهم دفعوا في الضلالة هداهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p98/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p98/r6.speaker: مالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p98/r6.claim: Mālik invokes the metaphor to bar a purchase option over items of one kind whose individual units differ and cannot lawfully be exchanged unequally.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p98/r6.anchor: تعلق مالك رحمه الله في منع أن يشتري الرجل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p98/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p98/r7.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p98/r7.claim: Some say the verse concerns a hypocrite who once believed, then inwardly apostatized; on this reading the transaction is nearly literal.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p98/r7.anchor: فيمن كان آمن من المنافقين ثم ارتد في باطنه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p98/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p98/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p98/r8.claim: “Their trade did not profit” closes the parable by echoing its opening image of purchase; profit is attributed to the trade, as in Arabic expressions “a standing night” and “a fasting day.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p98/r8.anchor: ختم للمثل بما يشبه مبدأه في لفظة الشراء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p98/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p98/r9.speaker: إبراهيم بن أبي عبلة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p98/r9.claim: Ibrāhīm b. Abī ʿAbla reads “their trades” in the plural.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p98/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p98/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p98/r10.claim: “They were not guided” may refer to this transaction, be a general description, or refer to God's prior knowledge; the wording permits all three.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p98/r10.anchor: وما كانوا مهتدين قيل المعنى في شرائهم هذا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p37/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p37/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p37/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿud and Ibn ʿAbbas say the verse was revealed concerning all unbelievers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p37/r1.anchor: نزلت في جميع الكفار قاله ابن مسعود وابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p37/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p37/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p37/r2.claim: Qatada, al-Suddi, and Muqatil say it concerns the People of the Book.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p37/r2.anchor: أنها في أهل الكتاب قاله قتادة والسدي ومقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p37/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p37/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p37/r4.claim: Here “bought” means exchanged: Arabic calls someone who prefers one thing a buyer of it and seller of the other; dalāla and ḍalāl both mean misguidance.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p37/r4.anchor: واشتروا بمعنى استبدلوا والعرب تجعل من آثر شيئا على شئ مشتريا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p37/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p37/r5.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p37/r5.claim: Al-Hasan, Qatada, and al-Suddi take the exchanged misguidance to mean unbelief and the guidance to mean faith.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p37/r5.anchor: أن المارد هاهنا الكفر والمراد بالهدى الإيمان روي عن الحسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p37/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p37/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p37/r6.claim: A second interpretation takes misguidance as doubt and guidance as certainty.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p37/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p37/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p37/r7.claim: A third interpretation takes misguidance as ignorance and guidance as knowledge.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p37/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p37/r8.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p37/r8.claim: Mujahid explains the exchange as people who first believed and then disbelieved.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p37/r8.anchor: أنهم آمنوا ثم كفروا قاله مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p37/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p37/r9.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p37/r9.claim: Muqatil says the Jews believed in the Prophet before his mission, then disbelieved in him when he was sent.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p37/r9.anchor: أن اليهود آمنوا بالنبي قبل مبعثه فلما بعث كفروا به قاله مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p37/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p37/r10.speaker: علي بن عبيد الله
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p37/r10.claim: The author’s teacher ʿAli ibn ʿUbayd Allah says those who rejected the Prophet’s guidance effectively traded it for misguidance.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p37/r10.anchor: الضلال كانو كمن أبدل شيئا بشئ ذكره شيخنا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p38/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p38/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p38/r1.claim: “Their trade did not profit” is figurative: trade itself does not profit; the trader profits in it. The same construction appears at 34:33 and 47:21, and in the cited verse.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p38/r1.anchor: من مجاز الكلام لأن التجارة لا تربح وإنما يربح فيها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p38/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p38/r2.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p38/r2.claim: Al-Farra, Ibn Qutayba, and al-Zajjaj accept this figurative construction when the intended meaning is clear; it is invalid when a predicate is attached to something that cannot bear it and another meaning is intended.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p38/r2.anchor: و إلى هذا المعنى ذهب الفراء وابن قبية والزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p38/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p38/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p38/r3.claim: “They were not guided” is explained as lacking knowledge of God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p38/r3.anchor: وما كانوا في العلم بالله مهتدين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p38/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p38/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p38/r4.claim: Another explanation is that they were not guided out of misguidance.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p38/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p38/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p38/r5.claim: Another explanation is that they were not guided to the believers’ trade.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p38/r5.anchor: وما كانوا مهتدين إلى تجارة المؤمنين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p38/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p38/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p38/r6.claim: Another explanation is that they were not guided in their purchase of misguidance.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p38/r6.anchor: وما كانوا مهتدين في اشتراء الضلالة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p38/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p38/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p38/r7.claim: The fifth explanation says a trader may fail to profit yet remain rightly guided and blameless; denying both profit and guidance intensifies their condemnation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p38/r7.anchor: قد لا يربح التاجر ويكون على هدى من تجارته غير مستحق للذم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p185/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p185/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود وناس من الصحابة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p185/r1.claim: They explain the bargain as taking misguidance and abandoning guidance.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p185/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p185/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p185/r2.claim: Through Ibn Ishaq's route, the exchange means disbelief for faith.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p185/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {أولئك الذين اشتروا الضلالة بالهدى} أي: الكفر بالإيمان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p185/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p185/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p185/r3.claim: The hypocrites first believed and then disbelieved.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p185/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p185/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p185/r4.claim: They preferred misguidance over guidance, meaning disbelief over faith; Ibn Kathir compares this to Thamud's choice of blindness.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p185/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة: استحبوا الضلالة على الهدى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p185/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p185/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p185/r5.claim: The commentators' common point is that hypocrites exchanged guidance for error, whether they apostatized after belief or preferred error from the outset; they comprised different kinds.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p185/r5.anchor: أن المنافقين عدلوا عن الهدى إلى الضلال، واعتاضوا عن الهدى بالضلالة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p185/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p185/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p185/r6.claim: Their deal yielded no profit: their transaction failed, and their conduct was not rightly guided.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p185/r6.anchor: أي: ما ربحت صفقتهم في هذه البيعة، {وما كانوا مهتدين} أي: راشدين في صنيعهم ذلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p185/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p185/r7.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p185/r7.claim: He describes them as moving from guidance to error, unity to division, security to fear, and Sunnah to innovation; Ibn Abi Hatim transmits the same report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p185/r7.anchor: خرجوا من الهدى إلى الضلالة، ومن الجماعة إلى الفرقة

JISHUMI:v1p259#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p259#2/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p259#2/r1.claim: The common reading has plural wāw and singular ‘trade’; reported variants alter the wāw's vowel or pluralize trade, but are rejected for lacking widespread transmission; fatḥ on wāw can be confused with dual marking.
JISHUMI:v1p259#2/r1.anchor: قراءة العامة: اشتروا بضم الواو، وتجارتهم على الواحد، وفتح الراء

JISHUMI:v1p259#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p259#2/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p259#2/r2.claim: Buying fundamentally means exchange: اشترى commonly means bought and شرى sold, although اشتريت can also mean sold; a sale is an exchange contract with legal conditions.
JISHUMI:v1p259#2/r2.anchor: أصل الشراء: الاستبدال، يقال: اشترى إذا ابتاع، وشرى إذا باع

JISHUMI:v1p259#2/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p259#2/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p259#2/r3.claim: Profit is the increase over capital, and trade is pursuing profit through sale; تجار is the plural of تاجر.
JISHUMI:v1p259#2/r3.anchor: والربح: الزيادة على رأس المال، ربح يربح

JISHUMI:v1p259#2/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p259#2/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p259#2/r4.claim: Misguidance originally means destruction and can mean leading from religion, judging someone astray, or losing the way to reward and Paradise; attributing misguidance to God is figurative except leading from religion, which is morally wrong.
JISHUMI:v1p259#2/r4.anchor: والضلال: أصله الهلاك، ثم يستعمل في معان

JISHUMI:v1p259#2/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p259#2/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p259#2/r5.claim: Plural wāw takes ḍamma after two silent letters because it signals plurality; لو استطعنا instead keeps the basic linking vowel.
JISHUMI:v1p259#2/r5.anchor: لما كانت الواو من علامة الجمع كان الضم أدل عليها

JISHUMI:v1p261/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p261/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p261/r1.claim: The fāʾ in ‘their trade did not profit’ reflects an implied conditional: if they exchanged guidance for error, their trade did not profit.
JISHUMI:v1p261/r1.anchor: لأن في الكلام معنى الجزاء وجوابه، كأنه قال: إذا اشتروا الضلالة بالهدى

JISHUMI:v1p261/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p261/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p261/r2.claim: The verse describes hypocrites as exchanging disbelief for faith; the author surveys seven explanations for how this applies if they never possessed guidance.
JISHUMI:v1p261/r2.anchor: ثم بين تعالى ما هم عليه من الضلالة والخسران، فقال: أولئك يعني المنافقين

JISHUMI:v1p261/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p261/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p261/r3.claim: One explanation takes ‘bought’ to mean chose and preferred, though this is not the apparent Arabic meaning.
JISHUMI:v1p261/r3.anchor: أن المراد ب اشتروا اختاروا واستحبوا؛ لأن كل مشتر مختار

JISHUMI:v1p261/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p261/r4.speaker: مجاهد
JISHUMI:v1p261/r4.claim: Mujahid says they believed and then disbelieved; the author rejects this as unsupported diversion from the wording and inconsistent with the passage.
JISHUMI:v1p261/r4.anchor: أنهم آمنوا ثم كفروا، فهو عموم أريد به الخصوص، عن مجاهد

JISHUMI:v1p261/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p261/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v1p261/r5.claim: The preferred view is that they abandoned faith for disbelief; it is reported from Ibn ʿAbbas, Ibn Masʿud, Abu ʿAli, and others.
JISHUMI:v1p261/r5.anchor: تركوا الإيمان إلى الكفر، واستبدلوه به، عن ابن عباس

JISHUMI:v1p261/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p261/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p261/r6.claim: They may have exchanged their innate disposition for disbelief, as described in a prophetic report.
JISHUMI:v1p261/r6.anchor: أنهم ولدوا على الفطرة كما جاء في الخبر، فتركوا ذلك إلى الكفر

JISHUMI:v1p261/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p261/r7.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
JISHUMI:v1p261/r7.claim: Before Muhammad's mission they believed in and foretold him; when he was sent, they rejected him and replaced that faith with disbelief.
JISHUMI:v1p261/r7.anchor: استبدلوا بالإيمان الذي كانوا عليه قبل البعثة؛ لأنهم كانوا يؤمنون بمحمد

JISHUMI:v1p261/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p261/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p261/r8.claim: Because disbelievers can choose either faith or disbelief, choosing disbelief is like exchanging faith for it.
JISHUMI:v1p261/r8.anchor: لما كان الكافر متمكنا منهما فاختار الكفر على الإيمان

JISHUMI:v1p261/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p261/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p261/r9.claim: A further explanation is that they professed faith outwardly and abandoned it inwardly.
JISHUMI:v1p261/r9.anchor: أنهم آمنوا ظاهرا، ثم تركوا الإيمان باطنا

JISHUMI:v1p261/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p261/r10.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
JISHUMI:v1p261/r10.claim: Most exegetes understand the exchange as disbelief for faith; Abu Muslim instead reads it as choosing punishment and destruction over guidance, Paradise, and reward.
JISHUMI:v1p261/r10.anchor: فقيل: الكفر بالإيمان، عن أكثر المفسرين، وقيل: اشتروا: اختاروا العذاب

JISHUMI:v1p261/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p261/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p261/r11.claim: ‘Their trade did not profit’ means they gained no benefit from their exchange.

SAMIN-DURR:2:16/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:16/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:16/r1.claim: أولئك is the subject and الذين with its relative clause is its predicate; فما ربحت تجارتهم is coordinated to the relative clause.
SAMIN-DURR:2:16/r1.anchor: " أولئك " رفع بالابتداء والذين وصلته خبره، وقوله تعالى:

SAMIN-DURR:2:16/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:16/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SAMIN-DURR:2:16/r2.claim: Some make فما ربحت تجارتهم the predicate of أولئك, with فاء licensed by the conditional force of الذين; the author rejects this because الذين is already the predicate.
SAMIN-DURR:2:16/r2.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أنها خبر المبتدأ، وأن الفاء دخلت في الخبر لما تضمنه الموصول

SAMIN-DURR:2:16/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:16/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:16/r3.claim: Making الذين a second subject leaves no link between أولئك and its predicate, and its past-tense relative clause also resists the proposal.
SAMIN-DURR:2:16/r3.anchor: يلزم من ذلك عدم الربط بين المبتدأ والجملة الواقعة خبرا عنه

SAMIN-DURR:2:16/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:16/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:16/r4.claim: Neither apposition nor adjective analysis works: it would pair a specific noun with another specific, and الذين is more definite than أولئك.
SAMIN-DURR:2:16/r4.anchor: وبأنه لا يجوز أن يكون وصفا له لأنه أعرف منه فبان فساد هذا القول

SAMIN-DURR:2:16/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:16/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:16/r5.claim: The usual damma on plural waw in اشتروا has been explained by analogy with subject tāʾ, distinction from root waw, ease, the deleted yāʾ vowel, or its plural meaning.
SAMIN-DURR:2:16/r5.anchor: والمشهور ضم واو " اشتروا " لالتقاء الساكنين، وإنما ضمت تشبيها

SAMIN-DURR:2:16/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:16/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:16/r6.claim: The waw is also read with kasra, its basic sukūn-junction vowel, or fatḥa, as lighter; al-Kisa'i's hamza is weak because its damma is not obligatory.
SAMIN-DURR:2:16/r6.anchor: وقرئ بكسرها على أصل التقاء الساكنين، وبفتحها: لأنه أخف

SAMIN-DURR:2:16/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:16/r7.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:16/r7.claim: Abu al-Baqa calls deletion of the waw's vowel by اختلاس extremely weak, since the preceding fatḥa cannot indicate it.
SAMIN-DURR:2:16/r7.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: " ومنهم من يختلسها، فيحذفها لالتقاء الساكنين وهو ضعيف جدا

SAMIN-DURR:2:16/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:16/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:16/r8.claim: اشتروا derives from استريوا: the moving yāʾ became alif and was deleted at two sukūns, or its vowel was removed and the yāʾ itself deleted.
SAMIN-DURR:2:16/r8.anchor: وأصل اشتروا: استريوا، فتحركت الياء وانفتح ما قبلها

SAMIN-DURR:2:16#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:16#2/r1.speaker: الكسائي
SAMIN-DURR:2:16#2/r1.claim: Al-Kisa'i's verse يا صباح لم تنام العشيا shows restoration of the alif after the plural waw receives an incidental vowel.
SAMIN-DURR:2:16#2/r1.anchor: فأعاد الألف لما حركت الميم حركة عارضة

SAMIN-DURR:2:16#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:16#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:16#2/r2.claim: الضلالة is the object and بالهدى is attached to اشتروا; باء here marks what was surrendered in an exchange.
SAMIN-DURR:2:16#2/r2.anchor: والباء هنا للعوض وهي تدخل على المتروك أبدا

SAMIN-DURR:2:16#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:16#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:16#2/r3.claim: شراء is metaphor for replacing guidance with error, reinforced by attributing profit to their trade, meaning they themselves did not profit.
SAMIN-DURR:2:16#2/r3.anchor: والشراء هنا مجاز عن الاستبدال بمعنى أنهم لما تركوا الهدى

SAMIN-DURR:2:16#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:16#2/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:16#2/r4.claim: In 4:74, where the apparent exchange acquires the hereafter, the addressed hypocritical laggards are urged to leave hypocrisy for faith and jihad, so the bā still marks what is left.
SAMIN-DURR:2:16#2/r4.anchor: فإن ظاهره أن الآخرة هي المأخوذة لا المتروكة، فالجواب ما قاله الزمخشري رحمه الله تعالى

SAMIN-DURR:2:16#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:16#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:16#2/r5.claim: Three unnamed poetic metaphors reinforce assigning an action to its object: silk weeps, a vulture and crow signify old age and youth, and Satan entering a burrow is expelled from another opening.
SAMIN-DURR:2:16#2/r5.anchor: لما أسند البكاء إلى الخز من أجل هذا الرجل

SAMIN-DURR:2:16#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:16#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:16#3/r1.claim: وما كانوا مهتدين is coordinated with فما ربحت تجارتهم; ربح means increase over capital, and مهتد is an active participle.
SAMIN-DURR:2:16#3/r1.anchor: هذه الجملة معطوفة على قوله: { فما ربحت تجارتهم } ، والربح: الزيادة على رأس المال

SAMIN-DURR:2:16#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:16#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:16#3/r2.claim: Here افتعل marks responsiveness to a transitive فعل, and this pattern only has that function with a transitive base.
SAMIN-DURR:2:16#3/r2.anchor: وافتعل هنا للمطاوعة، ولا يكون افتعل للمطاوعة إلا من فعل متعد.

SAMIN-DURR:2:16#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:16#3/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SAMIN-DURR:2:16#3/r3.claim: A grammarian claims اشتال is the responsive form of intransitive شال, citing a poet's اشتال سهيل; the author says it simply means the basic فعل.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p79/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p79/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p79/r1.claim: Here misguidance means unbelief and guidance means faith.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p79/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p79/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p79/r2.claim: One reading takes the purchase literally, as if they exchanged faith for unbelief, though hypocrites had not actually believed so as to sell faith.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p79/r2.anchor: أنه على حقيقة الشراء فكأنهم اشتروا الكفر بالإيمان

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p79/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p79/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p79/r3.claim: Another reading treats purchase as preferring unbelief to faith, since a buyer chooses what he favors.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p79/r3.anchor: أنه بمعنى استحبوا الكفر على الإيمان , فعبر عنه بالشراء

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p79/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p79/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p79/r4.claim: They took unbelief and abandoned faith.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p79/r4.anchor: أنه بمعنى أخذوا الكفر وتركوا الإيمان , وهذا قول ابن عباس وابن مسعود

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p79/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p79/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p79/r5.claim: The phrase may mean they were not rightly guided in purchasing misguidance.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p79/r5.anchor: وما كانوا مهتدين , في اشتراء الضلالة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p79/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p79/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p79/r6.claim: It may mean they were not guided to the profitable trade that believers found.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p79/r6.anchor: وما كانوا مهتدين إلى التجارة التي اهتدى إليها المؤمنون

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p79/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p79/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p79/r7.claim: The verse denies both profit and guidance to intensify blame, since a trader can fail to profit yet still be guided in the trade.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p79/r7.anchor: لما كان التاجر قد لا يربح , ويكون على هدى في تجارته نفى الله عنهم الأمرين

MUJAHID:v1p70/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p70/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p70/r1.claim: He interprets buying misguidance for guidance as believing and then disbelieving.
MUJAHID:v1p70/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد [ في قوله ] ﴿ اشتروا الضلالة بالهدى ﴾ يقول آمنوا ثم كفروا

MUQATIL:2:16/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:16/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:16/r1.claim: The Jews had found Muhammad’s description in the Torah and believed before his mission, expecting an Isaacite prophet; out of envy they rejected the Ishmaelite Muhammad and exchanged faith for denial, making a losing trade without guidance.
MUQATIL:2:16/r1.anchor: فآمنوا به وظنوا أنه من ولد إسحاق، عليه السلام، فلما بعث محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم من العرب

NASAFI-FULL:v1p20#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p20#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p20#2/r1.claim: They exchanged guidance for misguidance, choosing error in its place.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p20#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p20#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p20#2/r2.claim: One interpretation identifies people who believed and later disbelieved; another identifies Jews who believed in Muḥammad and then rejected him.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p20#2/r2.anchor: لأنها فى قوم آمنوا ثم كفروا أو فى اليهود الذين كانوا مؤمنين بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم فلما جاءهم كفروا به

NASAFI-FULL:v1p20#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p20#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p20#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, guidance was so available to them that it is depicted as already established within them before they left it for error.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p20#2/r3.anchor: أو جعلوا لتمكنهم منه كأن الهدى قائم فيهم فتركوه بالضلالة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p20#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p20#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p20#2/r4.claim: The trade metaphor supports the validity of a sale by mutual action without spoken offer and acceptance, when one takes an item and leaves its agreed price.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p20#2/r4.anchor: وفيه دليل على جواز البيع تعاطيا لأنهم لم يتلفظوا بلفظ الشرا ولكن تركوا الهدى بالضلالة عن اختيارهم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p20#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p20#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p20#2/r5.claim: Ḍalāla is deviation from the intended path or loss of guidance, metaphorically applied to religious error.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p20#2/r5.anchor: والضلالة الجور عن القصد وفقد الاهتداء يقال ضل منزله فاستعير للذهاب عن الصواب فى الدين

NASAFI-FULL:v1p20#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p20#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p20#2/r6.claim: Attributing profit to trade is figurative; extending the buying metaphor with profit and trade is rhetorical reinforcement, illustrated by a poem extending its raven-and-eagle comparison with nests.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p20#2/r6.anchor: وإسناد الربح إلى التجارة من الإسناد المجازي ومعناه فما ربحوا فى تجارتهم إذ التجارة لا تربح

NASAFI-FULL:v1p20#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p20#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p20#2/r7.claim: Their being unguided means they do not know profitable and loss-making commercial routes; their capital was guidance, which they lost for error.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p20#2/r7.anchor: لطرق التجارة كما يكون التجار المتصرفون العالمون

NASAFI-FULL:v1p20#2/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p20#2/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p20#2/r8.claim: The trader seeks preservation of capital and profit, but they lost both; worldly gains cannot count as profit when guidance is gone.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p20#2/r8.anchor: أن مطلوب التجار سلامة رأس المال والربح وهؤلاء قد أضاعوهما فرأس مالهم الهدى

NASAFI-FULL:v1p20#2/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p20#2/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p20#2/r9.claim: A grammatical alternative makes all of الذين a modifier of أولئك and the rest of the verse its predicate.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p20#2/r9.anchor: وقيل الذين صفة أولئك وفما ربحت تجارتهم إلى آخر الآية فى محل الرفع خبر أولئك

QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r1.speaker: سيبويه
QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r1.claim: The waw in اشتروا takes ḍamma to distinguish it from an original waw, as in a verse from Sūrat al-Jinn.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r1.anchor: قال سيبويه: ضمت الواو في «اشتروا» فرقا بينها وبين الواو الأصلية

QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r2.speaker: ابن كيسان
QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r2.claim: He says ḍamma is lightest on waw because the vowel is of its own kind.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r2.anchor: وقال ابن كيسان: الضمة في الواو أخف من غيرها لأنها من جنسها.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r3.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r3.claim: He explains the waw's ḍamma by analogy with نحن.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r3.anchor: وقال الزجاج: حركت بالضم كما فعل في «نحن».

QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r4.speaker: ابن أبي إسحق ويحيى بن يعمر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r4.claim: They read the waw with kasra, following the original rule for two adjoining quiescent letters.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي إسحق ويحيى بن يعمر بكسر الواو على أصل التقاء الساكنين.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r5.speaker: أبو زيد الأنصاري عن قعنب أبي السمال العدوي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r5.claim: He transmits a fatḥa reading, chosen for lightness even though the preceding letter is fatḥa.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r5.anchor: وروى أبو زيد الأنصاري عن قعنب أبي السمال العدوي أنه قرأ بفتح الواو

QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r6.speaker: الكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r6.claim: He permits hamza on the waw with ḍamma, like أدؤر.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r6.anchor: وأجاز الكسائي همز الواو وضمها كأدؤر.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r7.claim: Buying is metaphorical: they preferred disbelief to faith, since a buyer chooses what he wants; this is not an actual sale of faith they had possessed.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r7.anchor: والشراء هنا مستعار. والمعنى استحبوا الكفر على الإيمان

QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r8.claim: He glosses the exchange as taking misguidance and abandoning guidance, that is, choosing disbelief over faith.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: أخذوا الضلالة وتركوا الهدى. ومعناه استبدلوا واختاروا الكفر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r9.claim: The purchase wording is an expansive metaphor because Arabs use buying and trade for any substitution; the cited line describes trading forbearance for ignorance.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r9.anchor: لأن الشراء والتجارة راجعان إلى الاستبدال والعرب تستعمل ذلك في كل من استبدل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r10.claim: ضلالة primarily means bewilderment; forgetting is called misguidance because it involves confusion.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r10.anchor: وأصل الضلالة: الحيرة. ويسمى النسيان ضلالة لما فيه من الحيرة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r11.claim: Misguidance can also mean destruction, as in the question about being lost in the earth.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r11.anchor:
ويسمى الهلاك ضلالة كما قال عز وجل:
وقالوا أإذا ضللنا في الأرض

QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r12.claim: Attributing profit to the trade follows Arabic idiom; the intended meaning is that the traders themselves made no profit.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r12.anchor: أسند تعالى الربح إلى التجارة على عادة العرب في قولهم: ربح بيعك، وخسرت صفقتك

QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r13.speaker: ابن كيسان
QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r13.claim: He allows the plurals تجائر for تجارة and ضلائل for ضلالة.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r13.anchor: ابن كيسان: ويجوز تجارة وتجائر، وضلالة وضلائل.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r14.claim: They were not guided in choosing misguidance.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r14.anchor: وما كانوا مهتدين } في اشترائهم الضلالة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r15.speaker: قول
QURTUBI-FULL:2:16/r15.claim: Another explanation is that their lack of guidance was already present in God's prior knowledge.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:31/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:31/r9.speaker: الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:6:31/r9.claim: Al-Tabari takes the pronoun to refer to a transaction: they regret trading faith for disbelief and the afterlife for worldly life, as the loss-of-trade wording in al-Baqara indicates.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:31/r9.anchor: وقال الطبري: الهاء راجعة إلى الصفقة، وذلك أنهم لما تبين لهم خسران صفقتهم

STUDYQURAN:2:16/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:16/r1.speaker: Ṭ, R, Q
STUDYQURAN:2:16/r1.claim: They read purchased as preferred, comparable to choosing blindness over guidance in 41:17.
STUDYQURAN:2:16/r1.anchor: Here purchased can be understood as “preferred,” as in 41:17, they preferred blindness to guidance

STUDYQURAN:2:16/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:16/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:16/r2.claim: The commerce imagery makes the interpretation preferred less likely, despite its fit with an Arabic use of shirāʾ.
STUDYQURAN:2:16/r2.anchor: though this reading is made less likely by the mention of commerce

STUDYQURAN:2:16/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:16/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:16/r3.claim: The Quran elsewhere uses buying and selling as metaphors for spiritual matters.
STUDYQURAN:2:16/r3.anchor: Such language relating buying and selling to spiritual matters is also found in 2:86; 2:175; 3:177

TAB-FULL:v1p325/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p325/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p325/r1.claim: Buying misguidance for guidance means exchanging disbelief for faith.

TAB-FULL:v1p325/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p325/r2.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v1p325/r2.claim: The hypocrites took misguidance and abandoned guidance.

TAB-FULL:v1p325/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p325/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v1p325/r4.claim: They had believed and then disbelieved.

TAB-FULL:v1p325/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p325/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p325/r5.claim: Those who say they took misguidance and left guidance treat guidance as the price surrendered for the misguidance acquired.
TAB-FULL:v1p325/r5.anchor: الهدى الذي تركاه هو الثمن الذي جعلاه عوضا من الضلالة

TAB-FULL:v1p325/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p325/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p325/r6.claim: Those who read buying as preferring understand the phrase as choosing misguidance over guidance, with ba and ʿala sometimes substituting and ishtara used for choosing.
TAB-FULL:v1p325/r6.anchor: أولئك الذين اختاروا الضلالة على الهدى

TAB-FULL:v1p328/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p328/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p328/r1.claim: The cited al-Aʿsha line uses مشتراة for a woman chosen and brought out of seclusion, supporting the sense of buying as choosing.
TAB-FULL:v1p328/r1.anchor: فقد أخرج الكاعب المشتراة من خدرها وأشيع القمارا

TAB-FULL:v1p328/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p328/r2.speaker: ذو الرمة
TAB-FULL:v1p328/r2.claim: Dhu al-Rumma uses شراة for chosen ones, supporting the interpretation of ishtira as selection.
TAB-FULL:v1p328/r2.anchor: وقال ذو الرمة في الاشتراء بمعنى الاختيار

TAB-FULL:v1p328/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p328/r3.speaker: شاعر
TAB-FULL:v1p328/r3.claim: An unnamed poet likewise calls the choicest property شراة, illustrating choice rather than a literal transaction.
TAB-FULL:v1p328/r3.anchor: وقال آخر في مثل ذلك: [البحر السريع] إن الشراة روقة

TAB-FULL:v1p328/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p328/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p328/r4.claim: Al-Tabari rejects the choice interpretation because the following statement that their trade did not profit points to an actual exchange of one thing for another.
TAB-FULL:v1p328/r4.anchor: فدل بذلك على أن معنى قوله

TAB-FULL:v1p328/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p328/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p328/r5.claim: Although a literal exchange would fit people who first believed and then disbelieved, the opening description shows these hypocrites never entered Islam; their profession of faith was a lie.
TAB-FULL:v1p328/r5.anchor: ومن الناس من يقول آمنا بالله وباليوم الآخر وما هم بمؤمنين

TAB-FULL:v1p328/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p328/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p328/r6.claim: The purchase wording alone cannot prove prior faith, since buying can mean acquiring something by leaving another thing or choosing it.
TAB-FULL:v1p328/r6.anchor: الاشتراء عند مخالفيه قد يكون أخذ شيء بترك آخر غيره

TAB-FULL:v1p330/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p330/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p330/r1.claim: By trading guidance for misguidance, hypocrites lost: they exchanged clarity and security for confusion, blindness, fear, and terror now, as well as punishment later.
TAB-FULL:v1p330/r1.anchor: اختارا الحيرة والعمى على الرشاد والهدى والخوف والرعب على الحفظ والأمن

TAB-FULL:v1p330/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p330/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v1p330/r2.claim: They moved from guidance to error, unity to division, security to fear, and Sunnah to innovation.
TAB-FULL:v1p330/r2.anchor: خرجوا من الهدى إلى الضلالة، ومن الجماعة إلى الفرقة

TAB-FULL:v1p330/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p330/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p330/r3.claim: The expression their trade did not profit means they themselves made no profit; Arabic idiom can attribute an action to its setting and omit what listeners readily supply.
TAB-FULL:v1p330/r3.anchor: وإنما معنى ذلك: فما ربحوا في تجارتهم لا فيما اشتروا

TAB-FULL:v1p330/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p330/r4.speaker: الشاعر
TAB-FULL:v1p330/r4.claim: A cited poetic line says the worst fate is a man dying among his family, omitting the understood noun death.
TAB-FULL:v1p330/r4.anchor: كما قال الشاعر: [البحر الطويل] وشر المنايا

TAB-FULL:v1p332/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p332/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p332/r1.claim: The continuation of the cited line attributes sleeping to the night while meaning that the person himself slept, illustrating the idiom’s omitted subject.

TAB-FULL:v1p332/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p332/r2.speaker: جرير بن الخطفي
TAB-FULL:v1p332/r2.claim: Jarir attributes blindness and sight to day and night while describing the man, another example of attributing an action to its setting.
TAB-FULL:v1p332/r2.anchor: قال جرير بن الخطفي: [البحر الطويل] وأعور من نبهان أما نهاره

TAB-FULL:v3p67#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p67#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p67#2/r1.claim: Al-Tabari notes that he has already explained the purchase metaphor and the differing interpretations, so he does not repeat that argument here.
TAB-FULL:v3p67#2/r1.anchor: وكذلك بينا وجه: {اشتروا الضلالة بالهدى} [البقرة: 16] باختلاف المختلفين

ZAJJAJ:v1p89/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p89/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p89/r1.claim: The pronoun نحن is built on ḍamma because its plural marker is wāw, whose vowel is of the same kind; the wāw of a plural verb likewise takes ḍamma when moved to avoid two sukūns.
ZAJJAJ:v1p89/r1.anchor: نحن مبنية عفى الضم، لأن نحن يدل على الجماعة، وجماعة المضمرين يدل عليهم

ZAJJAJ:v1p89/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p89/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p89/r2.claim: Some pronounce اشتروا with kasra to resolve adjacent sukūns across words; the agreed reading has ḍamma, while a fatḥa reading is also reported as extremely anomalous.
ZAJJAJ:v1p89/r2.anchor: والقراءة المجمع عليها: (اشتروا الضلالة) بالضم، وقد رويت: (اشتروا الضلالة)، بالفتح، وهو شاذ جدا

ZAJJAJ:v1p89/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p89/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p89/r3.claim: The good reading of مستهزئون fully articulates the hamza; when lightened, it falls between wāw and hamza.
ZAJJAJ:v1p89/r3.anchor: القراءة الجيدة فيه، تحقيق الهمزة فإذا خففت الهمزة جعلت الهمزة بين الواو، والهمزة

ZAJJAJ:v1p89/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p89/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p89/r4.claim: The hamza in مستهزئون may be replaced by yāʾ, yielding مستهزيون; مستهزون is weak except as an anomalous dialect that changes hamza to yāʾ.
ZAJJAJ:v1p89/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن تبدل من الهمزة ياء فتقول: " مستهزيون "

ZAJJAJ:v1p91/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p91/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p91/r1.claim: يمدهم means ‘gives them respite,’ and طغيانهم means their excess and unbelief.
ZAJJAJ:v1p91/r1.anchor: معنى (ويمدهم) يمهلهم، وهو يدل على الجواب الأول.

ZAJJAJ:v1p91/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p91/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p91/r2.claim: يعمهون means they wander in confusion; عمه and عامه describe a confused person.
ZAJJAJ:v1p91/r2.anchor: ومعنى يعمهون في اللغة يتحيرون، يقال رجل عمه وعامه، أي متحير

ZAJJAJ:v1p91/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p91/r3.speaker: الراجز
ZAJJAJ:v1p91/r3.claim: An anonymous rajaz poet uses العمه for confused people who are blind to guidance, illustrating the sense of يعمهون.
ZAJJAJ:v1p91/r3.anchor: ومهمه أطرافه في مهمه. . . أعمى الهدى بالجاهلين العمه

ZAJJAJ:v1p91/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p91/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p91/r4.claim: أولئك is nominative as the subject, with الذين اشتروا الضلالة as its predicate.
ZAJJAJ:v1p91/r4.anchor: أولئك موضعه رفع بالابتداء وخبره (الذين اشتروا الضلالة)

ZAJJAJ:v1p91/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p91/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p91/r5.claim: Hamzating the wāw of اشتروا is mistaken: its ḍamma only resolves adjacent sukūns, unlike fixed-root ḍamma in أقتت and أدور; the same applies to لتبلون.
ZAJJAJ:v1p91/r5.anchor: لأن الواو المضمومة التي تبدل منها همزة إنما يفعل بها ذلك إذا لزمت صفتها

ZAJJAJ:v1p91/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p91/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p91/r6.claim: The Arabs call choosing one thing and abandoning another ‘buying’ it, although no actual sale occurs, because commitment to it resembles a purchaser’s desire.
ZAJJAJ:v1p91/r6.anchor: كل من ترك شيئا وتمسك بغيره فالعرب تقول للذي تمسك به قد اشتراه، وليس ثم شراء ولا بيع

ZAJJAJ:v1p91/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p91/r7.speaker: الشاعر
ZAJJAJ:v1p91/r7.claim: An unnamed poet uses اشترى figuratively of the unbeliever who adopts Christianity, illustrating ‘buying’ by choosing and adhering to something.
ZAJJAJ:v1p91/r7.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
اخدت بالجمة رأسا أزعرا. . . وبالثنايا الواضحات الدردرا
وبالطويل العمر عمرا أقصرا. . . كما اشترى الكافر إذ تنصرا

ZAJJAJ:v1p92/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p92/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p92/r1.claim: ‘Their trade did not profit’ means that they themselves gained no profit from it; Arabic attributes profit to the trade as a concise expression, as it also says ‘your sale lost.’
ZAJJAJ:v1p92/r1.anchor: معناه فما ربحوا في تجارتهم، لأن التجارة لا تربح وإنما يربح فيها ويوضع فيها

ZAJJAJ:v1p92/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p92/r2.speaker: الشاعر
ZAJJAJ:v1p92/r2.claim: An unnamed poet’s ‘his intimacy like Abu Marhab’s’ omits the implied noun خلالة, illustrating concise attribution by omission.
ZAJJAJ:v1p92/r2.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
وكيف تواصل من أصبحت. . . خلالته كأبي مرحب

ZAJJAJ:v1p92/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p92/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p92/r3.claim: The phrase بل مكر الليل والنهار means their plotting during night and day, since night and day themselves do not plot.
ZAJJAJ:v1p92/r3.anchor: (بل مكر الليل والنهار) (والليل والنهار لا يمكران) إنما معناه بل مكرهم في الليل

TABRISI:2:16/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:16/r1.speaker: جميع القراء
TABRISI:2:16/r1.claim: All canonical readers put ḍamma on the wāw of اشتروا.
TABRISI:2:16/r1.anchor: قرأ جميع القراء اشتروا الضلالة بضم الواو

TABRISI:2:16/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:16/r2.speaker: يحيى بن يعمر
TABRISI:2:16/r2.claim: In a noncanonical reading, Yaḥyā b. Yaʿmar gives the wāw kasra by analogy with the wāw in لو.
TABRISI:2:16/r2.anchor: وفي الشواذ عن يحيى بن يعمر أنه كسرها تشبيها بواو لو

TABRISI:2:16/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:16/r3.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب
TABRISI:2:16/r3.claim: Yaḥyā b. Waththāb is reported to give the wāw of لو ḍamma by analogy with the plural wāw.
TABRISI:2:16/r3.anchor: وروي عن يحيى بن وثاب أنه ضم واو لو تشبيها بواو الجمع

TABRISI:2:16/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:16/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:16/r4.claim: The wāw is vowelled after dropping the alif of the article brings two sukūns together; ḍamma distinguishes it from لو and أو and signals plurality.
TABRISI:2:16/r4.anchor: فحرك الأول منهما لالتقائهما وصار الضم أولى بها ليفصل بالضم

TABRISI:2:16/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:16/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:16/r5.claim: The analogy among wāw forms is like analogical case alternations in الضارب الرجل and الحسن الوجه.
TABRISI:2:16/r5.anchor: ومثل هذا إجازتهم الجر في الضارب الرجل تشبيها بالحسن الوجه

TABRISI:2:16/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:16/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:16/r6.claim: Purchase means exchange; Arabs also call choosing and holding one thing while leaving another a purchase, as the cited poem shows.
TABRISI:2:16/r6.anchor: حقيقة الاشتراء الاستبدال والعرب تقول لمن تمسك بشيء وترك غيره قد اشتراه

TABRISI:2:16/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:16/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:16/r7.claim: Profit is growth over capital; trade is seeking profit through sale, and Arabic may attribute profit or loss directly to the sale or trade.
TABRISI:2:16/r7.anchor: والتجارة التعرض للربح في البيع وقوله فما ربحت تجارتهم

TABRISI:2:16/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:16/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:16/r8.claim: أولئك begins the sentence, while الذين اشتروا is its predicate; with كان, مهتدين is its predicate and the plural ending derives historically from مهتديين.
TABRISI:2:16/r8.anchor: أولئك موضعه رفع بالابتداء وخبره الذين اشتروا الضلالة بالهدى

TABRISI:2:16/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:16/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:16/r9.claim: كان may denote only time and require a predicate, or be a full verb denoting both time and an event, as in the cited 2:282 phrase.
TABRISI:2:16/r9.anchor: والآخر من نحوى كان ما هو فعل حقيقي يدل على زمان وحدث

TABRISI:2:16#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:16#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:2:16#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the exchange as taking misguidance and abandoning guidance, meaning replacing faith with unbelief.
TABRISI:2:16#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس أخذوا الضلالة وتركوا الهدى ومعناه استبدلوا الكفر بالإيمان

TABRISI:2:16#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:16#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:2:16#2/r2.claim: Qatāda says they preferred and chose misguidance, since a buyer prefers what the other party holds.

TABRISI:2:16#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:16#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:16#2/r3.claim: One explanation is that they were born on the primordial disposition and then left it for unbelief, as the report says.
TABRISI:2:16#2/r3.anchor: أنهم ولدوا على الفطرة كما جاء في الخبر فتركوا ذلك إلى الكفر

TABRISI:2:16#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:16#2/r4.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
TABRISI:2:16#2/r4.claim: Al-Kalbī and Muqātil say they had believed in and expected Muhammad before his mission, then exchanged that faith for unbelief when he was sent.

TABRISI:2:16#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:16#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:16#2/r5.claim: Their trade failed: they replaced faith with unbelief and reward with punishment, and were not rightly guided as Muhammad's companions were.
TABRISI:2:16#2/r5.anchor: أي خسروا في استبدالهم الكفر بالإيمان والعذاب بالثواب

TABRISI:2:16#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:16#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:16#2/r6.claim: A further reading takes the verse as denying them both profit and guidance, since a trader can lose while still being guided.
TABRISI:2:16#2/r6.anchor: فإن التاجر قد يخسر ولا يربح ويكون على هدى

TABRISI:2:16#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:16#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:16#2/r7.claim: The mention of profit contrasts the exchange of misguidance for guidance with believers' profitable exchange of guidance for misguidance; in substance the hypocrites lose their capital.

THALABI:v1p158/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p158/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v1p158/r6.claim: They took misguidance and abandoned guidance, exchanging disbelief for faith.
THALABI:v1p158/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أخذوا الضلالة وتركوا الهدى

THALABI:v1p158/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p158/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p158/r7.claim: The trade metaphor figuratively means choosing and exchanging, since each buyer prefers what the other possesses; a poem likens it to a Muslim choosing Christianity.
THALABI:v1p158/r7.anchor: أخرجه بلفظ الشرى والتجارة توسعا لأن الشرى والتجارة راجعان إلى الاستبدال

THALABI:v1p158/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p158/r8.speaker: يحيى بن يعمر وابن أبي إسحاق
THALABI:v1p158/r8.claim: They read ishtaraw with kasra on the final waw, explaining the vowel as a lightening of the sukūn.
THALABI:v1p158/r8.anchor: يحيى بن يعمر وابن أبي إسحاق: اشتروا الضلالة بكسر الواو

THALABI:v1p158/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p158/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p158/r9.claim: Fama rabiHat tijaratuhum means they did not profit from their trade; Arabic can attribute profit to a sale, sleep to a night, and similar actions to their objects.
THALABI:v1p158/r9.anchor:
فما ربحت تجارتهم: أي فما ربحوا في تجارتهم.
تقول العرب: ربح بيعك

THALABI:v1p158/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p158/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p158/r10.claim: The idiom is supported by Qur'anic expressions about a matter being resolved and the plotting of night and day, and by a poem.
THALABI:v1p158/r10.anchor: فإذا عزم الأمر ، وقال: بل مكر الليل والنهار

THALABI:v1p159/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p159/r1.speaker: إبراهيم ابن أبي عبلة
THALABI:v1p159/r1.claim: He reads tijaratuhum in the plural, tijaratuhum.
THALABI:v1p159/r1.anchor: إبراهيم ابن أبي عبلة: (فما ربحت تجاراتهم) بالجمع

THALABI:v1p159/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p159/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p159/r2.claim: They were not guided out of misguidance and were not successful in their trade.
THALABI:v1p159/r2.anchor: وما كانوا مهتدين: من الضلالة، وقال: مصيبين في تجاراتهم

THALABI:v1p159/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p159/r3.speaker: سفيان الثوري
THALABI:v1p159/r3.claim: Everyone is a trader and should consider what trade he is making; the verse contrasts their failed trade with the trade that saves from painful punishment.
THALABI:v1p159/r3.anchor: سفيان الثوري: كلكم تاجر فلينظر امرؤ ما تجارته؟ قال الله فما ربحت تجارتهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p176#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p176#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p176#2/r1.claim: Purchase means exchange, but not every exchange is a purchase; using the purchase metaphor stresses eagerness, since the buyer wants what he takes and Arabic calls preference a sale even without an actual transaction.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p176#2/r1.anchor: حقيقة الاشتراء: الاستبدال، وكل اشتراء استبدال، وليس كل استبدال اشتراء،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p176#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p176#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p176#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the transaction as taking misguidance and leaving guidance.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p176#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس في هذه الآية: أخذوا الضلالة وتركوا الهدى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p176#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p176#2/r3.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p176#2/r3.claim: Scholars of meaning say the hypocrites never possessed guidance; they abandoned its obligation and replaced it with misguidance, so the verse describes them as buying it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p176#2/r3.anchor: قال أهل المعاني: هؤلاء المنافقون لم يكونوا على الهدى قط،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p176#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p176#2/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p176#2/r4.claim: Ishtaraw derives from ishtariyū; vowel change and deletion leave the plural wāw beside the silent definite article, requiring a linking vowel.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p176#2/r4.anchor: وأصل {اشتروا} اشتريوا، فلما تحركت (الياء) وانفتح ما قبلها صارت (ألفا)،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p176#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p176#2/r5.speaker: أكثر النحويين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p176#2/r5.claim: Most grammarians say plural wāws take ḍamma because it marks plurality; by contrast, nonplural wāws take kasra.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p176#2/r5.anchor: فقال أكثر النحويين: إن واوات الجمع كلها (¬4) تحرك بالضم نحو: {لتبلون}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p176#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p176#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p176#2/r6.claim: Some grammarians permit kasra by analogy with law and aw law, and also permit ḍamma in law istataʿnā by analogy with the plural wāw.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p176#2/r6.anchor: وقد أجازوا الكسر (¬1) في {اشتروا الضلالة} تشبيها بمثل: {لو استطعنا}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p176#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p176#2/r7.speaker: ناس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p176#2/r7.claim: Some say the wāw has ḍamma because it is semantically the subject; the author rejects this account, since an agentive yāʾ can take kasra and variants show the vowel is not inflection.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p176#2/r7.anchor: فجعلت حركة التقاء الساكنين فيه كحركة الإعراب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p179/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p179/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p179/r1.claim: Because some read the wāw with kasra here and in 2:237, the proposal that its vowel is like inflection cannot explain the variation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p179/r1.anchor: وقوم كسروا الواو في مسألتنا (¬8) وفي قوله: {ولا تنسوا الفضل بينكم}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p179/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p179/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p179/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the wāw receives the ḍamma that would belong to the verb’s final radical.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p179/r2.anchor: وقال الفراء: إنهم إنما حركوا (الواو) هاهنا بالحركة التي كانت تجب للام الفعل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p179/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p179/r3.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p179/r3.claim: Abū ʿAlī rejects al-Farrāʾ’s account: vowel transfer moves to a preceding consonant, not a following one, as the cited forms show.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p179/r3.anchor: قال أبو علي (¬4): الذي ذهب إليه الفراء هو أن الحركة في (الواو)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p179/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p179/r4.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p179/r4.claim: If al-Farrāʾ were right, the wāw would move regardless of what follows; in fact it moves only when two silent letters meet, proving this vowel breaks a meeting of sukūns.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p179/r4.anchor: فلما لم تتحرك الواو في {اشتروا} إلا عند التقاء ساكن، ثبت أن حركتها حركة الحروف الساكنة الملتقية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p179/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p179/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p179/r5.claim: Abū Isḥāq calls it mistaken to replace the wāw with hamza, since only a wāw whose ḍamma is fixed is hamzated; here the vowel is only for two adjacent sukūns.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p179/r5.anchor: قال أبو أسحاق: من أبدل واو (¬3) {اشتروا الضلالة} همزة، غالط

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p182/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p182/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p182/r1.claim: Ribḥ is increase over capital, and tijāra is circulating wealth to seek growth; a cited poem illustrates the verb tajara.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p182/r1.anchor: (الربح) الزيادة على أصل المال (¬7). و (التجارة) تقليب الأموال وتصريفها لطلب النماء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p182/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p182/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p182/r2.claim: The phrase means they did not profit from their trade; Arabs attribute profit to a transaction, as in common expressions, 34:33, 47:21, and Jarīr’s poem attributing blindness and sight to night and day.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p182/r2.anchor: ومعنى قوله {فما ربحت تجارتهم} أي ما ربحوا في تجارتهم، وأضاف الربح إلى التجارة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p182/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p182/r3.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p182/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ allows such attribution only when context makes the intended meaning clear; where ambiguous, a phrase like your servant lost could describe a trader or merchandise.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p182/r3.anchor: قال الفراء: وهذا إنما يجوز إذا عرف الكلام ولم يشكل، فإذا أشكل لم يجز

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:13-16/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:13-16/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:13-16/r4.claim: They chose error and abandoned guidance; their trade did not profit them. Attributing profit to the trade is expansive usage, like attributing illumination to fire, and they were not guided.

ELMALILI:2:16/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:16/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:16/r1.claim: The hypocrites exchanged guidance, which had been within their grasp, for misguidance; their trade yields no profit and they cannot find or follow a profitable path because they lost guidance, their greatest capital.
ELMALILI:2:16/r1.anchor: sermayelerin sermayesi olan hidâyeti vermiş yerine onun zayâ‘ı demek olan dalâleti almışlardır

ELMALILI:2:16/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:16/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:16/r2.claim: This verse parallels the description of the God-guided righteous in 2:5 and states the hypocrites' final condition; the trade metaphor reflects their familiar worldly concern and warns that religious guidance is prior to and necessary for sound worldly commerce.
ELMALILI:2:16/r2.anchor: Bu âyet müttakīn hakkındaki أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ عَلَىٰ هُدًۭى مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ âyetinin ‘adîli olarak
