ELMALILI:2:16/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:16/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:16/r3.claim: The image praises trade while teaching that its true path is sound understanding and uprightness: lying, deception, and intrigue cannot produce real profit, and religious guidance is needed to remain honest.
ELMALILI:2:16/r3.anchor: ticarette yalan, hud‘a, entrika yolunun hakīkī bir kâr yolu olmadığına tenbih

ELMALILI:2:16/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:16/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:16/r4.claim: Because hypocrites work from within to derail Islam's aims, believers need particular warning about them; four following verses make their loss tangible through parables and deter hypocrisy.
ELMALILI:2:16/r4.anchor: bir taraftan bunlar hakkında alenî kâfirden ziyade nazar-ı dikkati celb ile mü’minleri tenvir etmek

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:14/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:14/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:14/r3.claim: Those who consider themselves clever and believers foolish spend their life, reason, and will on misguidance instead of guidance and end their life's trade bankrupt.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:14/r3.anchor: kendilerini akıllı, iman edenleri de akılsız ve ahmak sananlar, kendilerine emanet edilen hayat, akıl ve irade sermayesiyle hidayet yerine sapkınlığı aldıkları için hayat ticaretini de iflasla kapatmaktadırlar

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p368#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p368#2/r1.speaker: أحمد بن موسى
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p368#2/r1.claim: All readers pronounce the plural waw in اشتروا with ḍamma.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p368#2/r1.anchor: قال أحمد بن موسى: ضم الواو اتفاق

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p368#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p368#2/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p368#2/r2.claim: When hamzat al-waṣl drops, the plural waw meets the article's silent lām; ḍamma resolves the two sukūns and is preferred to kasra to distinguish this waw from conjunction waw.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p368#2/r2.anchor: فصار الضم أولى بها ليفصل بالضم بينها وبين واو أو ولو

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p368#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p368#2/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p368#2/r3.claim: The unanimous ḍamma in لتبلون and لترون supports ḍamma here; مصطفو الله likewise shows the plural waw takes ḍamma, while cross-analogy with conjunction waw can license less apt alternatives.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p368#2/r3.anchor: اتفق الجميع فيه على التحريك بالضم دون غيره

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p370/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p370/r1.speaker: قوم
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p370/r1.claim: Some speakers replace the waw with hamza in اشترءوا, which Abu Ali treats as evidence that its ḍamma was established rather than alternating like an inflectional vowel.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p370/r1.anchor: أن قوما أبدلوا منها الهمزة، فقالوا: (اشترءوا الضلالة)

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p370/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p370/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p370/r2.claim: The hamza substitution does not prove the reading has a fixed ḍamma: the vowel is only inserted to resolve adjacent sukūns and is effectively a sukūn itself, from which hamza is not substituted.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p370/r2.anchor: والتحريك لالتقاء الساكنين في تقدير السكون لما تقدم من الدلالة على ذلك

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p370/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p370/r3.speaker: الفراء
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p370/r3.claim: Al-Farra, as reported by Ahmad ibn Yahya, says the plural waw takes the ḍamma that would belong to the verb's final radical.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p370/r3.anchor: وأما ما حكاه أحمد بن يحيى عن الفراء في أن قوله: (اشتروا الضلالة)

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p372/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p372/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p372/r1.claim: Al-Farra's transfer analysis fails because اشترى and اصطفى have final alif only through an assumed vowel; the alif remains as though bearing that vowel, so it cannot be transferred away.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p372/r1.anchor: إنما انقلبت اللام فيه ألفا لتقدير الحركة فيها، ولولا تقديرها لم تنقلب

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p372/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p372/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p372/r2.claim: Arabic transfers a vowel only to the preceding consonant, as in forms where a weak radical drops; it does not move that vowel to a later consonant, so the proposed transfer lacks a pattern.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p372/r2.anchor: ولا تنقل إلى ما بعد الحروف المنقولة منها الحركة

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p372/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p372/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p372/r3.claim: If the vowel were transferred from the final radical, the receiving waw or yāʾ would move whether or not another word followed; instead, it moves only before a separate sukūn, like other junction-induced vowels.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p372/r3.anchor: لا تتحرك حتى تلتقي مع ساكن منفصل منها دلالة على أنها تحركت

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p374/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p374/r1.speaker: نافع
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p374/r1.claim: The main transmission from Nafiʿ, followed by Qalun and Warsh, gives the alif-maqṣūra forms an intermediate sound between opening and imāla; al-Musayyibi reports that Nafiʿ opens them all.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p374/r1.anchor: والأول قول قالون وورش عن نافع

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p374/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p374/r2.speaker: ابن كثير
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p374/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir opens all the listed alif-maqṣūra forms.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p374/r2.anchor: وكان ابن كثير يفتح ذلك كله

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p374/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p374/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p374/r3.claim: Abu Amr uses intermediate imāla at verse endings but opens non-final forms; feminine forms on the listed faʿla patterns are also intermediate.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p374/r3.anchor: وأما أبو عمرو فكان يقرأ من ذلك ما كان من رءوس الآي بين الفتح والكسر

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p374/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p374/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p374/r4.claim: For Abu Amr, rāʾ before yāʾ is imālated; if that yāʾ disappears before a following consonant, imāla disappears. Two transmitters report broader imāla, but the known reading leaves it out.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p374/r4.anchor: والمعروف عن أبي عمرو ترك الإمالة في مثل: نرى الله جهرة

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p374/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p374/r5.speaker: عاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p374/r5.claim: Asim through Abu Bakr opens the forms except رأى، رمى، رآه، and نأى in al-Isra; he opens أعمى and the Sajda example, while a yāʾ-dropping junction produces imāla on rāʾ but opening on hamza.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p374/r5.anchor: وكان عاصم يفتح في رواية أبي بكر ذلك كله إلا: (رأى، ورمى ورآه)

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p54/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p54/r1.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p54/r1.claim: Transitive verbs predominate because a verb can describe either its agent or its object, while every verb requires an agent.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p54/r1.anchor: فكما لا بد للفعل من الفاعل، فكذلك كثر المتعدي

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p54/r2.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p54/r2.speaker: يحيى بن يعمر، ابن أبي إسحاق، أبو السمال
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p54/r2.claim: These readers are cited for a variant pronunciation of the plural waw in اشتروا; the waw has three dialectal vowels, with damma most common, then kasra, then fatha.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p54/r2.anchor: قراءة يحيى بن يعمر3 وابن أبي إسحاق وأبي السمال4

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p54/r3.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p54/r3.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p54/r3.claim: Damma best marks the plural waw apart from the waw in أو and لو, though some also use damma in لو and some Arabs give the plural waw kasra by analogy.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p54/r3.anchor: لأنها واو جمع، فأرادوا الفرق بينها وبين واو "أو" و"لو"

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p54/r4.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p54/r4.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p54/r4.claim: Fatha is least common because it is light beside the heavy waw and suffices to separate adjacent quiescent sounds; similar dialectal forms include قم الليل and قل الحق.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p54/r4.anchor: وأما الفتح فأقلها، والعذر فيه خفة الفتحة مع ثقل الواو

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p54/r5.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p54/r5.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p54/r5.claim: Some dialects hamza the waw in forms such as اشترءوا; Ibn Jinni treats this as a weak analogy that gives a temporary vowel the status of a permanent one.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p54/r5.anchor: ينبغي أن يكون ذلك على إجراء غير اللازم مجرى اللازم

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p54/r6.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p54/r6.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p54/r6.claim: When hesitating at a pause, speakers lengthen a final vowel and may create a matching glide, as in اشتروا, اشتروي, or اشتروا after the three waw vowels.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p54/r6.anchor: ولو وقفت مستذكرا وقد ضمت الواو؛ لقلت: اشترووا

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p71/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p71/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p71/r1.claim: For بالهدى, readers use full tafkhim, imāla, or an intermediate sound: tafkhim keeps the original articulation, while imāla brings the emphatic consonant toward yāʾ; Hamza distinguishes yāʾ-final from wāw-final forms.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p71/r1.anchor: فأما حمزة فأمال ذوات الياء وفخم ذوات الواو ليفرق بين المعنيين

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p71/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p71/r2.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p71/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir lengthens the pronoun hāʾ with a glide, using yāʾ after kasra and waw after damma; other readers indicate its vowel without adding a letter to avoid adjacent consonants around the weak hāʾ.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p71/r2.anchor: ابن كثير باشباع كسرة الهاء ووصلها بالياء

IBNMUJAHID:v1p144/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p144/r4.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p144/r4.claim: All agree on damma for the plural waw in اشتروا; the disagreement is in the imāla of بالهدى.

IBNMUJAHID:v1p144/r5.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p144/r5.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p144/r5.claim: Nafi has an intermediate reading on yāʾ-final forms; Qalun and Warsh support it, though al-Musayyibi reports that Nafi opens them throughout, as Ibn Kathir does.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p144/r5.anchor: والأول قول قالون وورش عن نافع

IBNMUJAHID:v1p144/r6.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p144/r6.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p144/r6.claim: Abu Amr uses an intermediate sound when the form ends an āya, but opens it elsewhere; feminine forms such as الدنيا and شتى remain between opening and imāla.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p144/r6.anchor: فإذا لم يكن رأس آية فتح مثل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p103/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p103/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p103/r6.claim: Ishtirāʾ and shirāʾ mean exchanging or acquiring by compensation; ribḥ is gain beyond capital, tijāra is managing money for growth, and muhtadī is form VIII as the responsive result of guiding someone, a use that requires a transitive base.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p103/r6.anchor: الاشتراء والشراء بمعنى: الاستبدال بالشيء والاعتياض منه، إلا أن الاشتراء يستعمل في الابتياع والبيع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p104/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p104/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p104/r1.claim: The poetic ishtāla is not evidence that form VIII can be responsive to an intransitive verb: it means the same as the simple verb shāla, so the form here is not reciprocal response.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p104/r1.anchor: لأن افتعل في البيت بمعنى، فعل. تقول: شال يشول، واشتال يشتال بمعنى واحد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p116/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p116/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p116/r5.claim: Ulaʾika points back to the hypocrites just described, who claimed reform, called believers foolish, and showed outward agreement while remaining with disbelievers; most readers use the damma in ishtaraw.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p116/r5.anchor: أولئك: اسم أشير به إلى الذين تقدم ذكرهم، الجامعين للأوصاف الذميمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p117/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p117/r1.speaker: أبو السماك قعنب العدوي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p117/r1.claim: Abu al-Sammak Qunab al-Adawi reads ishtaraw with fatḥa on the wāw; the customary damma has several syntactic explanations, while kasra is the basic response to two silent letters and fatḥa follows the preceding vowel.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p117/r1.anchor: وقرأ أبو السماك قعنب العدوي: اشتروا الضلالة بالفتح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p117/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p117/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p117/r2.claim: Hamza and al-Kisaʾi use imāla on al-hudā, the dialect of Banu Tamim; other readers use fatḥ, the Quraysh dialect.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p117/r2.anchor: وأمال حمزة والكسائي الهدى، وهي لغة بني تميم، والباقون بالفتح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p117/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p117/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p117/r3.claim: Abu Hayyan prefers a metaphorical reading of ishtaraw: choosing misguidance over guidance, since no actual counterparty receives an exchanged good; the metaphor treats the capacity to follow guidance as the purchase price.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p117/r3.anchor: والاشتراء هنا مجاز كنى به عن الاختيار، لأن المشتري للشيء مختار له مؤثر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p117/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p117/r4.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p117/r4.claim: Some argue literal exchange if the verse concerns hypocrites (Mujahid): their outward testimony and worship were guidance exchanged for disbelief, or their original fitra or capacity for sound reasoning was exchanged for desire and imitation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p117/r4.anchor: إن كان أراد بالآية المنافقين، كما قال مجاهد، فقد كان لهم هدى ظاهر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p117/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p117/r5.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p117/r5.claim: If the verse concerns People of the Book, as Qatada says, they expected the Prophet and believed in his coming, then rejected him to protect their status and income, supposedly exchanging belief for disbelief.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p117/r5.anchor: وإن كان أراد بالآية أهل الكتاب، كما قال قتادة، فقد كانوا مؤمنين بالله واليوم الآخر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p117/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p117/r6.speaker: ابن كيسان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p117/r6.claim: Ibn Kaysan says God created them for obedience, which they exchanged for disbelief; Abu Hayyan rejects this because a creation specifically for obedience could not fail to obey.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p117/r6.anchor: وقال ابن كيسان: خلقهم لطاعته، فاستبدلوا عن هذه الخلقة المرضية كفرهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p118/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p118/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p118/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, Hasan, Qatada, and al-Suddi identify misguidance with disbelief and guidance with faith; other explanations pair doubt with certainty, ignorance with knowledge, division with community, worldly life with the hereafter, or Hell with Paradise.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p118/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس، والحسن، وقتادة، والسدي: الضلالة: الكفر، والهدى: الإيمان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p118/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p118/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p118/r2.claim: The fāʾ in fa-mā rabiḥat shows the lack of profit follows the purchase immediately; Abu Hayyan rejects the claim that it marks a conditional result because alladhīna is the predicate of ulaʾika and fa-mā rabiḥat coordinates with the relative clause.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p118/r2.anchor: وهذا خطأ لأن الذين ليس مبتدأ، فيشبه بالشرط الذي يكون مبتدأ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p118/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p118/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p118/r3.claim: The sentence fa-lahum ajruhum is not a conditional answer, but the predicate of the subject al-ladhīna yunfiqūn; the proposed double-subject parses also fail for lack of a linking pronoun or because a past relative clause cannot take this fāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p118/r3.anchor: لأنه ليس بجواب، إنما الجملة خبر المبتدأ الذي هو ينفقون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p118/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p118/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p118/r4.claim: Ulaʾika is the subject and alladhīna the predicate; making alladhīna a separate subject or apposition fails syntactically and does not fit the verse's meaning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p118/r4.anchor: ولأن معنى الآية ليس إلا على كون أولئك مبتدأ والذين خبرا عنه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p118/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p118/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p118/r5.claim: Attributing profit to trade is metaphorical because traders, not trade itself, profit; the purchase metaphor is reinforced by describing the trade as failing, a figure that presents a metaphor as reality and then gives it a real attribute.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p118/r5.anchor: ونسبة الربح إلى التجارة من باب المجاز لأن الذي يربح أو يخسر إنما هو التاجر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p119/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p119/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p119/r1.claim: The cited line about the khazz fabric crying and rejecting its skin illustrates extending a metaphor by treating the fabric as a person; al-Shafiʿi similarly addresses gray hair as an owl that has nested on his head.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p119/r1.anchor: بكى الخز من روح وأنكر جلده ... وعجت عجيجا من جذام المطارف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p119/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p119/r2.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p119/r2.claim: Ibn Abi ʿAbla reads tijārātihim in the plural because each person has a separate trade; the majority read the singular collectively.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p119/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة: تجاراتهم، على الجمع، ووجهه أن لكل واحد تجارة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p119/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p119/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p119/r3.claim: The bare denial of profit might seem to imply their capital remained, since no profit does not itself mean a loss; the answer is that exchanging guidance for its opposite entails losing guidance altogether.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p119/r3.anchor: وفي قوله: فما ربحت تجارتهم، إشعار بأن رأس المال لم يذهب بالكلية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p119/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p119/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p119/r4.claim: Abu Hayyan also explains the denial through a figure like saying there is no road sign to follow: denying guidance can stand for the absence of the means to be guided.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p119/r4.anchor: ويتخرج عندي على أن يكون من باب قوله: علي لا حب لا يهتدي بمناره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p120/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p120/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p120/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says traders seek both safe capital and profit; the hypocrites lost guidance, their capital, and gained no true profit even if they obtained worldly goods, since a trader whose capital is gone has not profited.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p120/r1.anchor: سلامة رأس المال والربح، وهؤلاء قد أضاعوا الطلبتين معا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p120/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p120/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p120/r2.claim: Abu Hayyan finds that response inconclusive: denying profit alone does not prove that capital was lost or diminished, because profit is only the excess over capital.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p120/r2.anchor: ومع ذلك ليس بمخلص في الجواب لأن نفي الربح عن التجارة لا يدل على ذهاب كل المال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p120/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p120/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p120/r3.claim: Wa-mā kānū muhtadīn completes the meaning by stating what the denial of profit does not: that they lost their capital; this is rhetorical completion, illustrated by an Imruʾ al-Qays line.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p120/r3.anchor: قيل: لما لم يكن قوله تعالى: فما ربحت تجارتهم مفيدا لذهاب رؤوس أموالهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p120/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p120/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p120/r4.claim: The exchange is called trade though disbelief has no benefit because they believed or hoped for worldly and afterlife returns; groups claimed divine favor or that punishment would last only a few days, while disbelief nullifies deeds.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p120/r4.anchor: فلحصول الراحة الدنيوية ورجاء الراحة الأخروية، سمى اشتراءهم الضلالة بالهدى تجارة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p120/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p120/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p120/r5.claim: A hadith says that when asked whether Ibn Judʿan benefited from kinship and feeding the poor, the Prophet answered no because he never prayed for forgiveness on the Day of Judgment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p120/r5.anchor: وفي الحديث، أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم سئل عن ابن جدعان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p120/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p120/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p120/r6.claim: Possible senses of they were not guided include not being guided in God's knowledge, being unguided from error, lacking a profitable trade or a sound choice, or combining loss of profit with lack of guidance; some traders may fail to profit yet remain rightly guided.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p120/r6.anchor: وهل المعنى ما كانوا في علم الله مهتدين، أو مهتدين من الضلالة، أو للتجارة الرابحة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p120/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p120/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p120/r7.claim: Abu Hayyan prefers that they had never actually received guidance before, preventing the phrase bought guidance from implying that they once possessed it; the segment breaks as he begins to elaborate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p120/r7.anchor: والذي أختاره أن قوله تعالى: وما كانوا مهتدين إخبار بأن هؤلاء ما سبقت لهم هداية بالفعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p121/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p121/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p121/r1.claim: The exchange of guidance is metaphorical: they exchanged the capacity to apprehend guidance, whereas the closing denial concerns guidance actually attained.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p121/r1.anchor: بالهدى، ودل على أن الذي اعتاضوا الضلالة به إنما هو التمكن من إدراك الهدى، فالمثبت في الاعتياض غير المنفي أخيرا، لأن ذاك بالقوة وهذا بالفعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p121/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p121/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p121/r2.claim: مهتدين is the predicate of كان and is governed by كان alone.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p121/r2.anchor: وانتصاب مهتدين على أنه خبر كان، فهو منصوب بها وحدها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p121/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p121/r3.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p121/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ treats مهتدين as originally circumstantial because the subject is occupied by كان; its semantic usefulness lets it function as a definite predicate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p121/r3.anchor: وخلافا لمن زعم أن أصل انتصابه على الحال، وهو الفراء، قال: لشغل الاسم برفع كان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p121/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p121/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p121/r4.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects the circumstantial analysis attributed to al-Farrāʾ, preferring the straightforward predicate analysis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p121/r4.anchor: إلا أنه لما حصلت الفائدة من جهته كان حالا خبرا فأتى معرفة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p121/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p121/r5.speaker: المفسرون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p121/r5.claim: One reported occasion is that these verses were revealed about hypocrites generally.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p121/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p121/r6.speaker: المفسرون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p121/r6.claim: A second view says God described a people before they existed, thereby disclosing unseen knowledge.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p121/r6.anchor: في قوم أعلم الله بوصفهم قبل وجودهم، وفيه إعلام بالمغيبات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p121/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p121/r7.speaker: المفسرون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p121/r7.claim: A third view places the meeting verse in the story of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy and his companions, while the preceding passage concerns hypocrites generally; he praised Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, and ʿAlī to believers, then told his companions he had turned them away.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p121/r7.anchor: في عبد الله بن أبي وأصحابه نزل: وإذا لقوا الذين آمنوا والتي قبلها في جميع المنافقين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p160#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p160#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p160#2/r1.claim: Those referred to are the hypocrites described above: they claim rectitude while corrupting, call believers foolish while themselves foolish, and mock the mocked; the demonstrative marks their remoteness in evil.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p160#2/r1.anchor: إشارة إلى المنافقين الذين تقدم ذكرهم الجامعين للأوصاف الذميمة من دعوى الصلاح

ALUSI-FULL:v1p160#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p160#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p160#2/r2.claim: The purchase explains how their shameful traits arose: they chose error, lost their bargain, and wandered from the straight path; the sentence can also summarize their condition, explain the mockery, or confirm their being left to stray.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p160#2/r2.anchor: فإن السامع بعد سماع ذكرهم وإجراء تلك الأوصاف عليهم كأنه يسأل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p160#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p160#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p160#2/r3.claim: The relative description restricts the predicate rhetorically to these hypocrites because they excel in the combined enormity of their traits, although other unbelievers share in error.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p160#2/r3.anchor: وفيه حصر المسند على المسند إليه لكون تعريف الموصول للجنس بمنزلة تعيف اللام الجنسي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p160#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p160#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p160#2/r4.claim: Misguidance is deviation from the proper course and guidance is turning toward it; both also describe religious error and uprightness.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p160#2/r4.anchor: والضلالة الجور عن القصد والهدى التوجه إليه ويطلقان على العدول عن الصواب في الدين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p160#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p160#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p160#2/r5.claim: Since the hypocrites did not possess guidance as a literal purchase price, ishtirāʾ can mean choosing error over guidance; alternatively, they exchanged their full capacity and supporting means for guidance, or their innate fitra.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p160#2/r5.anchor: فأما أن يقال إن الإشتراء مجاز عن الأخيار لأن المشتري للشيء مختار له

ALUSI-FULL:v1p160#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p160#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p160#2/r6.claim: Al-Alusi rejects the Mufti's objection that innate guidance is common to everyone: these hypocrites first lost it through their parents' Judaizing, then squandered it through hypocrisy despite signs, instruction, and direct counsel.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p160#2/r6.anchor: إن الموصوفين بالنفاق المذكور هم الذين ضيعوا الفطرة أشد تضييع بتهويد الآباء

ALUSI-FULL:v1p160#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p160#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p160#2/r7.claim: The metaphor of purchasing is apt because they received overwhelming signs, miracles, admonition, and teaching that fully enabled guidance, but rejected them and fell into ruin.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p160#2/r7.anchor: لكنهم نبذوا ذلك فوقعوا في مهاوي المهالك

ALUSI-FULL:v1p161/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p161/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p161/r1.claim: Al-Alusi takes the purchased guidance to mean their belief in Muḥammad's advent and truth, which they found in the Torah and invoked before his coming; he rejects identifying it with outward prayer, almsgiving, fasting, and warfare.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p161/r1.anchor: والمراد بالهدى ما كانوا عليه من التصديق ببعثته

ALUSI-FULL:v1p161/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p161/r2.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
ALUSI-FULL:v1p161/r2.claim: Most exegetes, including Mujāhid, understand 'those' as the hypocrites; al-Alusi endorses this because it follows the immediate context.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p161/r2.anchor: هو الذي ذهب إليه أكثر المفسرين والمروي عن مجاهد

ALUSI-FULL:v1p161/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p161/r3.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v1p161/r3.claim: Qatāda reportedly applies the verse's demonstrative to the People of the Book generally; al-Alusi considers this interpretation distant as the occasion of the verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p161/r3.anchor: وروى عن قتادة أنهم أهل الكتاب مطلقا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p161/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p161/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v1p161/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Masʿūd reportedly take the referents as all unbelievers; al-Alusi rejects these as the intended referents, though the wording may apply to them too.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p161/r4.anchor: أن الآية بظاهر مفهومها تصدق على من أرادوا لا أن الآية نزلت فيهم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p161/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p161/r5.speaker: يحيى بن يعمر وابن إسحاق
ALUSI-FULL:v1p161/r5.claim: Yaḥyā b. Yaʿmar and Ibn Isḥāq read the initial hamza of 'they purchased' with kasra as the original vowel when two sukūns meet.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p161/r5.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن يعمر وإبن إسحاق ( أشتروا الضلالة ) بالكسر

ALUSI-FULL:v1p161/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p161/r6.speaker: أبو السماك
ALUSI-FULL:v1p161/r6.claim: Abū al-Sammāk reads the word with fatḥa by assimilation to the preceding vowel; Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī incline the alif of hudā according to Tamīm usage.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p161/r6.anchor: وأبو السماك ( أشتروا ) بالفتح إتباعا لما قبل وأمال حمزة والكسائي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p161/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p161/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p161/r7.claim: The fāʾ coordinates the loss of profit with the purchase as part of the relative clause; it signals the immediate consequence of the transaction, and al-Alusi rejects parses that make the relative clause an independent subject or predicate.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p161/r7.anchor: عطف على الصلة وأتى بالفاء للإشارة إلى تعقب نفي الربح للشراء

ALUSI-FULL:v1p162/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p162/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p162/r1.claim: The verse extends the trade metaphor: their lost guidance is capital and the missed benefits of guidance are profit, portraying their ruin as a merchant's worst loss.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p162/r1.anchor: وفي الآية ترشيح لما سمعت من المجاز فيما قبلها والمقصد الأصلي تصوير خسارهم بفوت الفوائد

ALUSI-FULL:v1p162/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p162/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p162/r2.claim: Attributing profit to the trade is metonymy for its owners; saying they did not profit implicitly condemns the loss and mocks their ignorance, while the following denial of guidance confirms actual loss rather than a neutral break-even result.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p162/r2.anchor: وإسناد الربح إلى التجارة وهو لأربابها ماجز للملابسة وكنى في مقام الذم ينفي الربح عن الخسران

ALUSI-FULL:v1p162/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p162/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p162/r3.claim: In ordinary trade a person may neither profit nor lose, but religious commerce has only guidance or misguidance; the context 'they were not guided' therefore marks the loss unmistakably.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p162/r3.anchor: والربح والخسران في الدين لا واسطة بينهما

ALUSI-FULL:v1p162/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p162/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p162/r4.claim: The clause 'they were not guided' most naturally coordinates with 'their trade did not profit'; it completes the implied loss and acts as rhetorical completion or intensification rather than needless repetition.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p162/r4.anchor: عطف على ما ربحت للقرب مع التناسب والتفرع بإعتبار المعنى الكنائي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p162/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p162/r5.speaker: الشريف
ALUSI-FULL:v1p162/r5.claim: Al-Sharīf prefers attaching 'they were not guided' to the earlier 'they purchased misguidance'; al-Alusi objects that this order is confusing and that the meanings are too close for a good conjunction.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p162/r5.anchor: وقال الشريف قدس سره : إن العطف

ALUSI-FULL:v1p162/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p162/r6.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
ALUSI-FULL:v1p162/r6.claim: Ibn Abī ʿAbla reads 'their trades' in the plural because each hypocrite has a trade; the majority's singular indicates that their many transactions form one common market.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p162/r6.anchor: وقرأ إبن أبي عبلة تجاراتهم على الجمع ووجهه أن لكل واحد تجارة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p162/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p162/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p162/r7.claim: A cited poetic line uses ishtāla for shāla yashūlu, showing an iftiʿāl form functioning like the simple verb.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p162/r7.anchor: حتى إذا أشتال سهيل في السحر كشعلة القابس ترمي بالشرر فأفتعل فيه بمعنى فعل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p68#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p68#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p68#2/r2.claim: Profit is attributed to the trade because Arabs idiomatically say that a sale profits or a transaction loses.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p68#2/r2.anchor: أضاف الربح إلى التجارة لأن الربح يكون فيها كما تقول العرب: ربح بيعك وخسرت صفقتك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p68#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p68#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p68#2/r3.claim: Not guided can mean that they were astray, or that they did not succeed in their trade.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p68#2/r3.anchor: {وما كانوا مهتدين} الضلالة، وقيل مصيبين في تجارتهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:16/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:16/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:16/r1.claim: They chose and exchanged misguidance for guidance; buying originally means paying a price to obtain a desired thing, and either side can be conceived as buyer or seller.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:16/r1.anchor: اختاروها عليه واستبدلوها به، وأصله بذل الثمن لتحصيل ما يطلب من الأعيان، فإن كان أحد العوضين ناضا

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:16/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:16/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:16/r2.claim: The commercial word extends to abandoning one thing to obtain another, including abstract meanings; a poem about a Muslim becoming Christian illustrates the usage.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:16/r2.anchor: ثم استعير للإعراض عما في يده محصلا به غيره، سواء كان من المعاني أو الأعيان، ومنه قول الشاعر:

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:16/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:16/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:16/r3.claim: They abandoned innate guidance given by God through human nature to obtain misguidance, or they preferred and desired misguidance over guidance.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:16/r3.anchor: المعنى أنهم أخلوا بالهدى الذي جعله الله لهم بالفطرة التي فطر الناس عليها محصلين الضلالة التي ذهبوا إليها. أو اختاروا الضلالة

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:16#2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:16#2/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:16#2/r1.claim: The profit-and-trade wording extends the buying metaphor and depicts their loss; an anonymous poetic example likewise sustains a metaphor.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:16#2/r1.anchor: ترشيح للمجاز، لما استعمل الاشتراء في معاملتهم أتبعه ما يشاكله تمثيلا لخسارتهم، ونحوه:

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:16#2/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:16#2/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:16#2/r2.claim: Trade seeks gain through buying and selling; profit is surplus over capital, and attributing it to trade is figurative because trade participates in or causes it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:16#2/r2.anchor: والتجارة: طلب الربح بالبيع والشراء. والربح: الفضل على رأس المال، ولذلك سمي شفا

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:16#2/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:16#2/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:16#2/r3.claim: They are unskilled in trade: their capital was sound nature and pure reason, but false beliefs ruined their capacity and left them unable to reach truth or perfection.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:16#2/r3.anchor: فإن المقصود منها سلامة رأس المال والربح، وهؤلاء قد أضاعوا الطلبتين لأن رأس مالهم كان الفطرة السليمة، والعقل الصرف

BIQAI-FULL:v1p45/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p45/r17.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p45/r17.claim: The buyers of misguidance persist in their desires, forcing themselves against the innate disposition God gave them despite the available evidence; they exchanged guidance, the axis of conscious good, for what is ugly.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p45/r17.anchor: لجوا في هواهم فكلفوا أنفسهم ضد ما فطرها الله عليه مع ما نصب من الأدلة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p45/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p45/r18.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p45/r18.claim: Their trade did not profit: they squandered their capital and retained only misguidance, which lowers its companion below animals despite their claim to discernment.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p45/r18.anchor: أضاعوا رأس المال , لأنه لم يبق في أيدهم غير الضلال الذي صاحبة في دون رتبة البهائم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p45/r19.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p45/r19.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p45/r19.claim: The author says he will explain in Joseph that the twelve forms of the root ش ر ي revolve around persistence or clinging.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p45/r19.anchor: وسيأتي في سورة يوسف عليه السلام بيان أن مادة شرى بتركيبها الاثنى عشر تدور على اللحاجة

DURR-FULL:v1p79/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p79/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p79/r5.claim: Buying misguidance for guidance means exchanging unbelief for faith.
DURR-FULL:v1p79/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {أولئك الذين اشتروا الضلالة بالهدى} قال: الكفر بالإيمان

DURR-FULL:v1p79/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p79/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v1p79/r6.claim: Ibn Masud explains the exchange as taking misguidance and abandoning guidance.
DURR-FULL:v1p79/r6.anchor: عن ابن مسعود في قوله {اشتروا الضلالة بالهدى} قال: أخذوا الضلالة تركوا الهدى

DURR-FULL:v1p79/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p79/r7.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p79/r7.claim: Mujahid says they first believed and then disbelieved.
DURR-FULL:v1p79/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {أولئك الذين اشتروا الضلالة بالهدى} قال: آمنوا ثم كفروا

DURR-FULL:v1p79/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p79/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p79/r8.claim: Qatada says they preferred error to guidance; their trade failed as they moved from guidance to error, unity to division, safety to fear, and Sunna to innovation.
DURR-FULL:v1p79/r8.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {أولئك الذين اشتروا الضلالة بالهدى} قال: استحبوا الضلال على الهدى {فما ربحت تجارتهم

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p494/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p494/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p494/r1.claim: In the usual Quranic construction, ب marks what is given up in a purchase; thus 2:175 depicts exchanging guidance for error and forgiveness for punishment.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p494/r1.anchor: يفيد سياقها في تسعة عشر موضعا أنها بمعنى الشراء، والباء فيها دخلت على المبيع المتروك

BURHAN:v2p255/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p255/r1.speaker: الجمهور
BURHAN:v2p255/r1.claim: The majority holds that metaphor occurs in the Qur'an.
BURHAN:v2p255/r1.anchor: والجمهور على الوقوع وأنكره جماعه منهم ابن القاص من الشافعية

BURHAN:v2p255/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p255/r2.speaker: ابن القاص وابن خويز منداد
BURHAN:v2p255/r2.claim: Ibn al-Qass, Ibn Khuwayz Mindad, and others deny Qur'anic metaphor: a speaker turns to metaphor only when literal expression is constrained, which they deem impossible for God.
BURHAN:v2p255/r2.anchor: وأنكره جماعه منهم ابن القاص من الشافعية وابن خويز منداد من المالكية

BURHAN:v2p255/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p255/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p255/r3.claim: The objection fails: excluding metaphor would also exclude emphasis, ellipsis, repeated narratives, and much of the Qur'an's beauty.
BURHAN:v2p255/r3.anchor: ولو وجب خلو القرآن من المجاز لوجب خلوه من التوكيد والحذف وتثنية القصص

BURHAN:v2p255/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p255/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p255/r4.claim: Abu Muhammad Ibn Abd al-Salam composed a separate work on metaphor and covered the subject comprehensively.
BURHAN:v2p255/r4.anchor: وقد افرده بالصنيف الإمام أبو محمد بن عبد السلام وجمع فأوعى

BURHAN:v2p255/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p255/r5.speaker: الحاتمي
BURHAN:v2p255/r5.claim: Al-Hatimi derives majaz as a verbal noun meaning the path or source of speech, by analogy with maqam from qumtu.
BURHAN:v2p255/r5.anchor: قال الحاتمي معناه طريق القول ومأخذه مصدر جزت مجازا كما يقال قمت مقاما

BURHAN:v2p255/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p255/r6.speaker: الأصمعي
BURHAN:v2p255/r6.claim: Al-Asma'i characterizes Arabic speech as formed through examples and likenesses.
BURHAN:v2p255/r6.anchor: قال الأصمعي كلام العرب إنما هو مثال شبه الوحي

BURHAN:v2p255/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p255/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p255/r7.claim: Metaphor has two causes: resemblance, called lexical metaphor and discussed by legal theorists, and association, called rational metaphor and discussed by linguists.
BURHAN:v2p255/r7.anchor: أحدهما الشبه ويسمى المجاز اللغوي وهو الذي يتكلم فيه الأصولي والثاني الملابسة

BURHAN:v2p255/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p255/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p255/r8.claim: Rational metaphor is attributing a word to something other than its proper subject through an interpretive relation, such as crediting a cause with an act.
BURHAN:v2p255/r8.anchor: وهو ان تسند الكلمة إلى غير ماهي له اصالة بضرب من التأويل كسب زيد اباه اذا كان سببا فيه

BURHAN:v2p255/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p255/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p255/r9.claim: The increase of faith is attributed to the recited verses, and ruin to a person's supposition, because each is a cause of the result.
BURHAN:v2p255/r9.anchor: ونسبت الزيادة التي هي فعل الله إلى الآيات لكونها سببا فيها

BURHAN:v2p255/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p255/r10.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p255/r10.claim: Slaughter is ascribed to Pharaoh as the one ordering it, while stripping is ascribed to Satan because his temptation caused the couple to eat.
BURHAN:v2p255/r10.anchor: والفاعل غيره ونسب الفعل اليه لكونه الآمر به

BURHAN:v2p255/r11.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p255/r11.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p255/r11.claim: The verse makes the trade itself the grammatical subject of profit, an example of rational metaphor.
BURHAN:v2p255/r11.anchor: وقوله تعالى ﴿ فما ربحت تجارتهم ﴾ جعل التجارة الرابحة

BURHAN:v2p255/r12.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p255/r12.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p255/r12.claim: In “when the matter is resolved,” the matter is what is resolved upon; the wording is clarified by the command to resolve and then rely on God.
BURHAN:v2p255/r12.anchor: وقوله ﴿ فإذا عزم الأمر ﴾ لآن الأمر هو المعزوم عليه

BURHAN:v2p255/r13.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p255/r13.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p255/r13.claim: The leaders are credited with bringing their people to ruin because their commands caused the people's disbelief.
BURHAN:v2p255/r13.anchor: فنسب الإحلال الذي هو فعل الله إلى اكابرهم لان سببه كفرهم وسبب كفرهم امر اكابرهم اياهم بالكفر

BURHAN:v4p405/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p405/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p405/r1.claim: The negative particle ma can precede nouns and verbs; with a noun it can work like laysa, raising the subject and putting the predicate in the accusative in Hijazi usage.
BURHAN:v4p405/r1.anchor: ففي الأسماء ك ليس ترفع وتنصب في لغة اهل الحجاز ووقع في القرآن في ثلاث مواضع

BURHAN:v4p405/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p405/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p405/r2.claim: With a past verb, ma has no grammatical effect and means lam, as in the verse's denial that their trade profited.
BURHAN:v4p405/r2.anchor: وعلى الأفعال فلا تعمل وتدخل على الماضي بمعنى لم نحو ما خرج أي لم يخرج

BURHAN:v4p405/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p405/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p405/r3.claim: Before an imperfect verb, ma negates the present, like la, denying that the act is occurring now.
BURHAN:v4p405/r3.anchor: وعلى المضارع لنفي الحال بمعنى لا نحو ما يخرج زيد اي لا يخرج نفيت أن يكون منه خروج في الحال

BURHAN:v4p405/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p405/r4.speaker: ابن الحاجب
BURHAN:v4p405/r4.claim: Ibn al-Hajib says ma negates the present in both Hijazi and Tamimi usage.
BURHAN:v4p405/r4.anchor: قال ابن الحاجب هي لنفي الحال في اللغتين الحجازية والتميمية نحو ما زيد منطلقا ومنطلق

BURHAN:v4p405/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p405/r5.speaker: ابن الحاجب
BURHAN:v4p405/r5.claim: Ibn al-Hajib allows ma to negate past or future when contextual clues establish that sense.
BURHAN:v4p405/r5.anchor: قال ابن الحاجب هي لنفي الحال في اللغتين الحجازية والتميمية نحو ما زيد منطلقا ومنطلق ولهذا جعلها سيبويه

BURHAN:v4p405/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p405/r6.speaker: سيبويه
BURHAN:v4p405/r6.claim: Sibawayh treats ma as an emphatic negative, parallel to qad in affirmative speech, since qad itself conveys emphasis and proximity to the present.
BURHAN:v4p405/r6.anchor: جعلها سيبويه في النفي جوابا لقد في الإثبات ولا ريب إن قد للتقريب من الحال

BURHAN:v4p405/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p405/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p405/r7.claim: Ma can negate a completed past, as in the unbelievers' claim that no bearer of good news or warning came; the context explains it as their future excuse after proof.
BURHAN:v4p405/r7.anchor: فإنه ورد للتعليل على معنى كراهة إن يقولوا عند إقامة الحجة عليهم

BURHAN:v4p405/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p405/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p405/r8.claim: The author gives a Qur'anic counting rule: ma followed by illa is negative in thirteen places, beginning with three examples listed from al-Baqara and al-Nisa.
BURHAN:v4p405/r8.anchor: وهنا ضابط وهو إذا ما اتت بعدها إلا في القرآن فهي من نفي إلا في ثلاثة عشر موضعا

BURHAN:v4p405/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p405/r9.speaker: بعضهم
BURHAN:v4p405/r9.claim: Some call the negative particle jaḥd, while others reject that label; the author notes that the distinction between jaḥd and negation was discussed earlier.
BURHAN:v4p405/r9.anchor: ومنهم من يسميه جحدا وأنكره بعضهم وسبق الفرق بين الجحد والنفي

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p227/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p227/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p227/r1.claim: Jurjānī calls attributional metaphor an independent treasure of eloquence, giving poets and skilled writers room for invention and breadth of expression.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p227/r1.anchor: هذا الضرب من المجاز على حدته كنز من كنوز البلاغة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p227/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p227/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p227/r2.claim: Familiar tropes such as longing “bringing” someone to a place only seem literal through common use; their subtlety demands literary skill.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p227/r2.anchor: يدق ويلطف حتى يمتنع مثله إلا على الشاعر المفلق

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p227/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p227/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p227/r3.claim: A figurative predicate need not always admit a paraphrase that restores its literal agent; “their trade profited” is one case where Jurjānī offers that conversion.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p227/r3.anchor: واعلم أنه ليس بواجب في هذا أن يكون للفعل فاعل في التقدير

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p228/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p228/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p228/r1.claim: Attributional figure is recognized when the action’s sense, such as arriving, becoming, or increasing, stays literal; the figure lies in its syntactic attribution.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p228/r1.anchor: فالاعتبار إذا بأن يكون المعنى الذي يرجع إليه الفعل موجودا في الكلام على حقيقته

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p228/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p228/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p228/r2.claim: Hājiz b. ʿAwf’s couplet describes a drought so severe that a hundred camels yield too little milk for one boy’s evening drink.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p228/r2.anchor: حتى إن جلب منها مئة لم يحصل من لبنها ما يكون غبوق غلام واحد

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p228/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p228/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p228/r3.claim: In the drought couplet, the verb for giving an evening drink remains literal; the figure is attributing that act to the camels.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p228/r3.anchor: وإنما المجاز في أن أسند إلى الإبل

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p315/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p315/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p315/r1.claim: Jurjānī rejects critics’ assumption that the verse’s altered case and omitted words leave meaning unchanged; its syntactic form contributes to its merit.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p315/r1.anchor: فيرى إعراب الاسم الذي هو التجارة قد تغير فصار مرفوعا بعد أن كان مجرورا

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p315/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p315/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p315/r2.claim: Fasāḥa has merit associated with lexical figures such as metonymy, metaphor, and representation, as well as merit associated with syntactic arrangement.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p315/r2.anchor: الكناية والاستعارة والتمثيل الكائن على حد الاستعارة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p315/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p315/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p315/r3.claim: Concrete idioms can move the listener more than plain paraphrases, as with “much ash” for generosity, “long sword-belt” for stature, or “lion” for a brave man.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p315/r3.anchor: كان له موقع وحظ من القبول لا يكون إذا قلت

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p492/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p492/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p492/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats buying misguidance for guidance and trading worldly life for the hereafter as metaphors for exchanging or giving one thing up for another.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p492/r5.anchor: وذهب الزمخشري إلى أن: من المجاز {اشْتَرَوُا الضَّلَالَةَ بِالْهُدَى} : استبدلوه

BAQILLANI:v1p76/r8.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p76/r8.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p76/r8.claim: The Qurʾānic description of error traded for guidance and an unprofitable trade is another metaphor.
BAQILLANI:v1p76/r8.anchor: اشتروا الضلالة بالهدى فما ربحت تجارتهم

BURHAN:v3p354/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p354/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p354/r4.claim: The four broken plural forms of paucity and the two sound plurals are inherently paucity forms; other plurals may indicate few or many as context determines, as Qur'anic examples show.
BURHAN:v3p354/r4.anchor: واعلم أن جموع التكثير الأربعة وجمعى التصحيح أعنى جمع التأنيث وجمع التذكير كل ذلك للقلة

ITQAN:v3p122/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p122/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p122/r1.claim: A reinforced metaphor is the strongest type: “buying” means choosing or exchanging, then “profit” and “trade” extend the imagery from the source domain.
ITQAN:v3p122/r1.anchor: فالأولى وهي أبلغها أن تقترن بما يلائم المستعار منه

ITQAN:v3p97/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p97/r15.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p97/r15.claim: Another subtype has figurative terms at both ends: “their trade did not profit” means they did not profit from it.
ITQAN:v3p97/r15.anchor: ثانيها مجازيان نحو ﴿ فما ربحت تجارتهم ﴾ أي ما ربحوا فيها وإطلاق الربح والتجارة هنا مجاز

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p373/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p373/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p373/r5.claim: A third Qur'anic sense is choosing, as in choosing error over guidance and buying distracting talk.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p373/r5.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الشرى في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p85/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p85/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p85/r4.claim: In فما ربحت تجارتهم, the merchants profit in their trade; the trade itself is not the agent that profits.
